robots.name: RVIR-CI / RobEnt
robots.full_name: RVIR-CI / RobEnt: BIT remote-controlled vascular interventional robot (catheter and guidewire cooperating on one rail; called RobEnt in the Tiantan clinical papers), with multilevel operation strategy
robots.group: Beijing Institute of Technology (Shuxiang Guo, Nan Xiao) with Kagawa University; clinical partners Beijing Neurosurgical Institute / Beijing Tiantan Hospital (Youxiang Li, Yuhua Jiang, Keyun Liu)
robots.versions: Kagawa remote catheter systems incl. remote angiography on a dog Kagawa-Beijing (chen2023_operating, secondary, ~2012) -> guo2016_design (MR-fluid force-feedback catheter system) -> bao2018_cooperation (RVIR-CI: catheter AND guidewire, 780 mm range) -> yang2019_vascular (fuzzy control, in vivo animal) -> bao2022_multilevel (three force zones, two haptic devices); isomorphic leader yang2022_isomorphic (full: real catheter and guidewire as handles on belt-coupled encoder platforms with linear-force and torque feedback, built after surgeons' feedback from in vivo experiments; Sec. 2-3); in-human operation evaluation bao2018_operation (Biomed. Microdevices 20:34, doi:10.1007/s10544-018-0277-5, title via Crossref, cited as ref. 13 of yang2022). Later BIT-Abrobo reciprocating robot (cao2024_reciprocating) became PANVIS-A: A4 scope, not catalogued here.; string-driven multi-slider slave with an optical-mouse master and kinetics + ADRC control (zhou2022_kinetics; its Sec. 2.2 says the slave was evaluated in bao2018_cooperation); RobEnt, the Tiantan team's name for the robot: first patient (jiang2018_initial, 2018) and ten pigs with micro-devices, a disposable waterproof cover and a sheath sleeve (liu2021_animal, 2021); 2011-15: J. Guo / N. Xiao (Kagawa-BIT) robotic catheter system with real-time force feedback: load cell + fibre-optic sensor (Guo 2011, 2012 ROBIO), Xiao 2012, push-force feedback with a mock-handle leader (Xiao 2015 ICIA) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 XI) (belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating; li2024_design); 2015: Jia / S. Guo (BIT) interventional surgical robot with force feedback, spur-gear rotation and torque-controlled gripper (Jia 2015 ROBIO; follow-ups Guo 2016, Wang 2018, Guo 2018) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 JI) (belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating); 2016: Bao / S. Guo guidewire navigation robot with fuzzy-PID force control (Bao 2016 ICMA; Guo 2016 ICMA) (Konda 2025 Table 2 row 13) (konda2025_robotically); 2018-20: Y. Zhao / S. Guo slave with on-line acquisition of the operating force by torque measurement (Zhao 2018 Biomed. Microdevices; 2019; 2020) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 ZH1) (belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating); 2022-24: C. Lyu / S. Guo robot with a flexible tactile-sensing gripper (FTG; lasso-style grip, force estimated from finger bending; Lyu 2023 RA-L) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 9 row 4, Figs. 10k, 14d) (alekseeva2025_design; li2024_design); 2020: N. Xiao (BIT) balloon-catheter delivery module with two geared conveyor belts on the lab's direct-push catheter/guidewire robot with joystick handles, bench (Yuan 2020 ICMA; host robot and operation logic Wang 2020 ICMA) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 4 row 4, Fig. 13b) (yuan2020_design; wang2020_reciprocating; alekseeva2025_design); 2018: S. Guo / N. Xiao (BIT) real-time master-slave (RTMS) system with closed-loop force feedback and a master handle that measures the surgeon's force (Guo 2018 Biomed. Microdevices 20, doi:10.1007/s10544-018-0278-4; Chen 2023 calls its guidewire mechanism heavy) (guo2018_realtime; chen2023_operating); 2019 and 2022: N. Xiao (BIT) sterile-side drive parts: bevel-gear catheter rotation structure for the guidewire operator (K. Wang 2019 ICMA) and a guidewire rotation-and-delivery transmission that limits slip (M. Cheng 2022 ICMA), both bench-tested for accuracy; Belikov codes the 2022 paper CHEs (wang2019_novel; cheng2022_novel; belikov2024_evolution); 2022-24: Y. Yan / S. Guo (BIT) 3-DoF slave with clamping-bracket grippers (PG2 SEA gripper, TIM 2023), grasping-force passive safety method with Changhai Hospital (TIM 2023) and an SEA haptic leader (ICRA 2024), ex vivo phantom per Alekseeva (Alekseeva 2025 Table 8 row 3, Fig. 10h) (alekseeva2025_design; yan2023_seabased; yan2023_grasping; yan2024_novel); 2022: deep-learning guidewire-compliant control (GCCM) run on the BIT endovascular surgery robot platform, slave rebuilt after Y. Zhao 2020 and Bao 2019, Geomagic Touch X leader, acrylic phantom, five operators: operating force -44.0 %, time -24.6 % (Lyu 2022 Micromachines; Konda 2025 control row 32) (lyu2022_deeplearningbased; konda2025_robotically); 2023: Y. Yan / S. Guo (BIT) spring-based tendon-driven steerable catheter for the group's master-slave robot: 1.5 mm active section (support spring with a 20 mm stainless-steel spine, one tendon, silicone coating) on a PTFE-lined passive section; the tendon pulled by a Maxon motor through a rack and pinion, displacement from the motor encoder; bench only, active section bent against a printed circle grid (radii 22.5 to 6 mm), bending radius from tendon displacement with mean absolute error 0.109 mm (6.53 %) (Yan 2023 ICMA, Secs. II-A, III, Figs. 8-10; Alekseeva 2025 Table 15 row 3) (yan2023_novel; alekseeva2025_design); RobEnt: robot of endovascular treatment with force feedback and cooperating catheter and guidewire (built by Beijing Institute of Technology; clinical team Beijing Neurosurgical Institute / Tiantan Hospital); BIT string-driven vascular intervention surgical robotic system (ADRC control)
robots.target_anatomy: neurovascular: cerebral angiography in a patient (bilateral carotid and vertebral arteries, jiang2018_initial); human body vessel model; pig aortic arch vessels ex vivo
robots.devices_driven: catheter (5 F tested) + guidewire (0.8 mm rod used in rotary test), driven simultaneously by two manipulators on one rail (bao2018 Sec. 4); first patient: 5 F 135-degree angiographic catheter (Cordis) and 0.035-in 150 cm hydrophilic guidewire (Terumo) (jiang2018_initial p. 2); 2021 animals: also Exel-14 microcatheter and 0.014-in micro-guidewire inside the 5 F catheter (liu2021_animal p. 2, 4)
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 (linear + rotary for each of catheter manipulator and guidewire manipulator; bao2018 Table 1)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp
robots.rotation_detail: Rotating conical-clamp grasper in each manipulator; assistant grasping mechanisms 1-3 on the rail hold the device while the manipulator returns (bao2018 Figs. 10, 12)
robots.device_range: 5 F catheter; guidewire ~0.8 mm (steel-rod test stand); no stated range limits; RobEnt 2018: travel 0.9 m, linear speed up to 90 cm/s, rotation up to 420 deg/s (jiang2018_initial p. 4); 2021: push 1.2 m, < 5 cm/s, < 180 deg/s (liu2021_animal p. 5)
robots.footprint_mm: rail travel 780 mm (bao2018 Sec. 4.1); overall size N.R.
robots.force_sensing: Proximal axial force per manipulator by strain-gauge sensor behind a low-friction bearing transmission (static connection, to avoid the slip of friction wheels): max relative error 2.53 % (catheter) / 2.48 % (guidewire) vs ATI reference (bao2018 Sec. 5.1). Tip contact: 1.3 mm fibre-optic pressure sensor in a 5 F catheter, 0-0.2 N (guo2019_novel Sec. IV-B).; RobEnt papers: force feedback on the console handle, resistance and vessel contact shown on the console, sensor type N.R. (jiang2018_initial p. 4)
robots.haptics_leader: Bao 2018/2022: two commercial haptic devices (Geomagic Touch X), one per device. Guo 2019: passive magnetorheological-fluid leader around a real 7 F input catheter. Yang 2022: isomorphic leader with real catheter and guidewire as handles. yang2022 detail: catheter and guidewire fixed on their own handle platforms, belt-coupled to encoder motors, with linear-force and torque feedback devices and eccentric force compensation (Sec. 3, Figs. 3-11).; first patient: console with two haptic handles outside the room (jiang2018_initial Fig. 1); zhou2022: optical-mouse master reading axial and circumferential displacement, force feedback N.R.
robots.imaging_compat: X-ray DSA (Siemens Artis zee III in 2018, AXIOM Artis dBA in 2021); robot not connected to the DSA (jiang2018_initial p. 4, 9)
robots.sterility: sterile membrane over the slave, sterilisation time < 1 h (jiang2018_initial p. 4, 6); 2021: disposable sterile waterproof transparent cover and a sleeve at the arterial sheath (liu2021_animal p. 6-7); conical clamp holds the device without damaging its surface (bao2018 Sec. 2.2)
robots.validation_detail: Human: 1 patient (chosen from 5 inpatients with suspected intracranial aneurysm), robot-driven cerebral angiography of both carotid and both vertebral arteries, about 40 min, no complication on 7.0 T MRI at 48 h or at the 7-day follow-up; Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Beijing; local ethics committee approval, no registration stated (jiang2018_initial Secs. 2-4). yang2022 Sec. 2 also cites clinical trials with this robot (Bao et al. 2018, Biomed. Microdevices 20:34, bao2018_operation, not read; patient count N.R.). Animal: 10 Bama miniature pigs (15-20 kg), at least three vessels each (liu2021_animal); pig in vivo trial (yang2019_vascular); dog remote test Kagawa-Beijing via the review chen2023_operating. Phantom: human-body vessel model (bao2018), in vitro model and ex vivo pig aortic arch (bao2022), vascular model 10 of 10 runs to the left subclavian artery (yang2022 Sec. 4.3), 2-D paraffin-wax model (zhou2022 Sec. 4).
robots.key_numbers: CM accuracy 0.11 +/- 0.023 mm and 1.43 +/- 0.30 deg; GM 0.12 +/- 0.024 mm and 1.43 +/- 0.28 deg (bao2018 Table 1); range 780 mm at 20 mm/s; max grip force/torque CM 20.2 N / 24.4 mN.m, GM 18.5 N / 21.6 mN.m; leader-follower mean displacement error 0.038-0.241 mm (bao2022 Sec. V); pig in vivo tracking mean 0.22 mm / 0.17 deg (chen2023_operating, secondary); jiang2018: procedure about 40 min, axial accuracy 0.2 mm, rotation 2 deg; liu2021: mean operation 38.8 min, catheter-guidewire switch 2.8 min, axial 0.1 mm, rotation 5 deg; zhou2022: maximum steady errors 0.45 mm and 6.67 deg with kinetics + ADRC
robots.sim_model: Not of the robot. Kagawa/BIT virtual-reality catheter-operation training simulators model catheter-vessel interaction (guo2012_virtual JRM; wang2016_virtual IJMRCAS, abstract level); no robot-drive simulator found.

robots.read_level_detail: full (bao2018_cooperation; yang2022_isomorphic; zhou2022_kinetics; jiang2018_initial; liu2021_animal); partial (bao2022, guo2019); abstract (yang2019); title (bao2018_operation in-human); secondary via review (dog test); full (yan2023_novel, version line)
robots.notes: Mechanism lesson stated in bao2018 Introduction: friction wheels slip, so proximal force is hard to measure; the group moved to conical-clamp graspers mounted on a force-sensing stage. ren2023_critical Table IV lists 'stroke 780 mm' for the BIT row, which matches bao2018 (the S8 evidence file could not find it in guo2019). | 2026-11-08 X3: highest_validation animal -> human on yang2022 Sec. 2 (clinical trials with this robot) + its ref. 13 (Bao 2018 in-human evaluation). robent_jiang2018 (X2 scope; Jiang, Liu, Li of Tiantan with BIT, first cerebral angiography, ABB 2018) is very likely the same BIT robot: coordinator to decide a merge. Bao 2018 in-human paper (Springer) not downloaded in this round | X4 2026-11-08: robent_jiang2018 and bit_stringdriven_zhou2022 merged into this row (data/merge_map.csv: same group, same one-rail slave, same room and slave in jiang2018 Fig. 1(b) and yang2019 Fig. 4). Category academic -> clinical-stage: a university robot that treated a first patient, filed like the Beihang, Hanyang and Asan robots (paper Secs. II, IV). | N4 2026-11-09: yan2023_novel read in full: the tendon is motor-driven (Sec. III, p. 770: 'actuated by a Maxon motor with a rack and pinion mechanism'), tested on the bench only (in air, against a circle grid; no vessel phantom in the paper, unlike Alekseeva's 'ex vivo phantom'); filed as a version line of this group's row, as Gao 2017 on sia_zhang2025; row cells unchanged; merged from robent_jiang2018 (A2); merged from bit_stringdriven_zhou2022 (A2)

robots.name: RAECS / ECRS
robots.full_name: Kagawa/BIT magnetorheological-fluid haptic master-slave catheter system (RAECS / ECRS)
robots.group: Kagawa University and Beijing Institute of Technology (Shuxiang Guo; Yu Song, Xuanchun Yin, Linshuai Zhang, Xingyu Li); later Chengdu University of Information Technology
robots.versions: guo2016_design (MR-fluid leader, force-sensor array) -> yin2018_magnetorheological (2-DOF slave, force sensing unit) -> song2018_performance -> guo2019_novel (T-RO: MR leader around a real catheter, fibre-optic tip sensor, collision zones) -> zhang2021_magnetorheological (catheter+guidewire system) -> li2022_collaborative (ECRS: collaborative handles, hydrogel + solid MR fluid, tremor-reduction structure) -> zhang2025_innovative (MRF master interface); 2007: S. Guo (Kagawa) "new catheter operating system" (Guo, Kondo, Wang, Guo, Tamiya 2007, ICME; Rafii-Tari 2014 Table 4 row 2) (rafiitari2014_current); 2014-21: J. Guo / S. Guo grasper-type slave (Belikov GU2.1-2.3): 2014 grasper, 2019 wedge-block guidewire clamp (ICMA), 2020 fuzzy PID, 2021 pinion fixture (ICMA), Liao 2022 (Alekseeva 2025 Table 6 row 5, Fig. 10f) (alekseeva2025_design; belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating; li2024_design); 2006: Harbin Engineering University with S. Guo, master-slave catheter driving mechanism for intravascular neurosurgery, two stepping motors (disk gear rotation, gear-pair axial drive), Internet remote control, bench precision test of a 2 mm catheter with a laser displacement sensor (Feng 2006 ICMA) (Zhao 2022 Table 1 row 24; Li 2024 Fig. 5A) (feng2006_highly; zhao2022_remote; li2024_design)
robots.target_anatomy: cerebrovascular / general (endovascular evaluator model)
robots.devices_driven: guo2016: catheter on a slave whose insertion angle adjusts 0-45 deg (guo2016 Sec. 2.4); yin2018 and guo2019: one 5 F patient catheter (7 F input catheter at the leader); zhang2021: catheter or guidewire held by an electromagnetic adaptive collet (Sec. 3, Fig. 4); li2022: 5 Fr catheter and 260 cm J-type guidewire at once, catheter and guidewire manipulation units (CMU, GMU) (Sec. 2.2, 4.4)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 for the catheter (axial, radial; guo2016, yin2018, guo2019); li2022 CMU + GMU move catheter and guidewire separately (count N.R.)
robots.translation_detail: clamp-relay (guo2019: platform on two stepper motors, grasper A holds for insertion/retraction/rotation while grasper B holds the catheter during A's return; axial grip force 4 N, S8 reading of Sec. II-B)
robots.rotation_detail: Rotation of the holding grasper (radial DOF)
robots.footprint_mm: li2022 slave: 920 mm overall length, 400 mm CMU/GMU travel (Sec. 2.2); earlier versions N.R.
robots.force_sensing: Load cell on the follower for proximal force; 1.3 mm fibre-optic pressure sensor in a 5 F catheter for tip contact force, working range 0-0.2 N (guo2019 Sec. IV-B); guo2016: load cell on the driven module behind grasper 1, plus a tip force-sensor array; zhang2021: load cell under the clamp; li2022: two TEAC TU-UJ load cells (+/-5 N) and two torque sensors for radial torque (Sec. 2.2)
robots.haptics_leader: Passive MR-fluid haptic interface around the real input catheter; resistance up to ~0.5 N at 150 mT (0.4 N at 110 mT); three levels switched at tip forces 0.08, 0.10, 0.12 N (guo2019); ten operators noticed the step at 150 mT in 93 % of trials
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.validation_detail: In vitro only: guo2016 tracking and force-feedback benches with a vascular model; yin2018 ten novice volunteers drove a 5 Fr catheter through a rigid cerebral model into a wide-neck aneurysm; guo2019 ten operators in the EVE model; zhang2021 ten non-medical subjects in the EVE model with collision cues; li2022 tracking tests and six trialists inserting a guidewire into the EVE model with and without haptics; zhang2025 volunteers reaching targets along a 15 cm vascular-model path (Sec. 4 of each)
robots.key_numbers: guo2019: axial positioning error 1.23 +/- 0.07 mm, rotation 1.57 +/- 0.07 deg; li2022: mean translation tracking error 0.94 mm, rotation 0.89 deg (abstract); MR resistance 0.16-0.5 N across 30-150 mT; guo2016: axial tracking error < 2 mm; zhang2021: axial transmission error < 1 mm (10 runs), 5 Fr catheter driven at 3.5 mm/s in the force test; li2022: CMU/GMU stepping motors 0.36 deg resolution
robots.sim_model: VR catheter-operation simulators from the same group (guo2012_virtual; wang2016_virtual); no physics model of the follower found

robots.name: SIAT haptic robot
robots.full_name: SIAT third-generation isomorphic primary-secondary robotic catheter system with haptic-enabled primary (clamp-relay secondary manipulator, magnetic-powder-brake primary interface)
robots.group: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, CAS (Lei Wang, Hongbo Wang, Olatunji Omisore) with Fudan University (Wenke Duan)
robots.versions: third generation cited to 2022 (du2024 Sec. II-A ref. [25], Du et al., T-MRB 2022; not read) -> 2024 improved prototype that logs proximal and distal force, 168 trials by surgeons and novices in a coronary phantom (du2024_analyzing, full) -> 2024 4-DoF slave-side device in a white branded housing on an arm, PID gains tuned by deep RL in a CoppeliaSim model (omisore2024_sample, full) -> 2025 primary haptic interface with magnetic powder brake and a resistance-detection module on the clamp (duan2025_development, ToH 2025)
robots.target_anatomy: cardiovascular model with pulse pump (right coronary artery, stenoses)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire / catheter (one tool at a time; sizes N.R.): guidewire through a guiding catheter into the anterior descending branch (du2024 Sec. II-B); "flexible endovascular tools such as catheter and guidewire" (omisore2024 Sec. II)
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 on the secondary manipulator (clamping, delivery, rotation, orientation adjustment; duan2025 Sec. II-B); "a robotic 4-DoF mechanism", of which axial translation and axial rotation are used (omisore2024 Sec. II-A)
robots.translation_detail: clamp-relay
robots.rotation_detail: Rotation module with self-aligning roller bearing and four balance springs (mechanism details N.R.) du2024 and omisore2024 defer the drive mechanism to earlier papers (du2024 Sec. II-D ref. [29]; omisore2024 Sec. II-A ref. [20]).
robots.footprint_mm: 570 x 220 x 160 (slave-side device; omisore2024 Sec. II-A: "57x22x16 cm"); secondary travel 150 mm per stroke (duan2025 Sec. II-B)
robots.force_sensing: Proximal vessel-tool interaction force: axial resistance pushes the tool against clamp A, which compresses a bearing plate on LFS-13-10N sensors (Ligent, Shenzhen) 2024 prototype (du2024 Sec. II-A, II-D3 to II-D5): proximal axial force sensor on the secondary's slider (SBT674-2kg, range 19.6 N) measures friction plus tool-tissue force; a 32-channel flexible pressure sensor on the primary control ring (0.01-19.6 N) measures the operator's finger force; distal tool-tissue force comes from a 6-axis F/T sensor (SBT308, 49 N per axis, composite error 1.0 %) under the phantom, not on the robot. omisore2024 Sec. II-A: "in-built sensing units for position and force feedback".
robots.haptics_leader: Primary interface with magnetic powder brake; dynamic hysteresis compensation model; human-perception-based haptic enhancement amplifying low-force changes and a safety strategy The 2024 primary uses the same motion sensors as the 2025 interface (magnetostrictive position sensor SDM20T-0150, rotary encoder E40H12-1000-3; du2024 Sec. II-D, duan2025 Sec. II-A); du2024 renders no force to the operator. omisore2024: master with a control knob and potentiometer, commands over TCP/IP with about 0.1 s delay (Sec. II-A, IV-C).
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.validation_detail: Haptic force calibration, then robot-assisted catheterisation in a cardiovascular model; human-subject study approved by SIAT-IRB-220915-H0606 (participant count not extracted) du2024: 168 robot-assisted trials, 12 per subject, in a 1:1 adult vascular simulator with pulsatile blood-like fluid; path with one branch, two stenoses (37.45 %, 42.69 %) and a tortuous part; group A 10 subjects without and group B 5 with manual PCI experience (168 / 12 = 14, so Sec. II-B and II-E2 disagree on the count); same IRB approval SIAT-IRB-220915-H0606 (du2024 p. 1, Sec. II-B, II-E2). omisore2024: bench only, 1 mm displacement commands on the slave-side device, number of runs N.R. (Sec. IV-C, Fig. 7).
robots.key_numbers: Stroke 150 mm; haptic enhancement and hysteresis compensation as the stated contributions; no headline error numbers extracted du2024: CNN recognition of operator-robot cooperation 99.99 % (test set); synergy ratios 89.66 %, 90.28 % and 91.12 % "based on the three aspects of delay consideration" for experienced operators; constant delay modelled as 0.254 s (Abstract, Sec. III). omisore2024: on the robot, displacement error within +/-2 x 10^-2 mm (Sec. IV-C, Fig. 7); in CoppeliaSim, DRL-PID error 0.003 +/- 0.0058 mm vs 0.012 +/- 0.009 (Ziegler-Nichols PID) and 0.015 +/- 0.011 mm (fuzzy PID), 10 trials of 100 set-points each (Sec. IV-B).
robots.sim_model: CoppeliaSim model of the slave-side robot: Solidworks CAD exported as URDF, prismatic and revolute joints for axial translation and rotation with parameterised static and dynamic variables and simulated position sensors; no vessel or device model (omisore2024_sample Sec. III-A, Fig. 3)

robots.versions: choi2021_vascular (Biosensors 2021); 2017-18: Asan (J. Choi) EP platform driving a commercial ablation (steerable) catheter with rolling belts, leader with a 3-RRR planar manipulator (Moon 2018), ex vivo phantom (Hu 2017) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 3 row 7, Fig. 8f; Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 HU1) (alekseeva2025_design; belikov2024_evolution); 2020-21: Asan (J. Choi, Y.-H. Kim) cardiac-ablation catheter robot: dual-gripper front module inserts and rotates the catheter without slip, handle module turns the bending knob, Jacobian updated from two position sensors on the catheter (Lee 2021 J. Mech. Robot. 13, doi:10.1115/1.4048224) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 LE) (lee2021_design; belikov2024_evolution); 2021: deep RL (Rainbow) guidewire navigation trained and tested on the physical 2-D and 3-D coronary phantoms with an Asan robotic module whose opposed roller pair advances the wire and whose vertical roller shift rotates it, step 0.4 mm or 33 deg (Kweon 2021 IEEE Access; Konda 2025 control row 33); real-world training, not sim-to-real (kweon2021_deep; konda2025_robotically)
robots.target_anatomy: coronary (PCI)
robots.devices_driven: three modules drive a guiding catheter, a guidewire and a balloon catheter (Sec. 2.1.2, p. 3), 3 devices at once; the clamping also fits guide extensions and IVUS catheters (p. 2); bench devices 5 F catheter, 0.014-in guidewire, 3.5 x 15 mm balloon (p. 10); in vivo only the guidewire was robot-driven (p. 13-16)
robots.n_dof_detail: 8 by our sum (paper gives no total): guiding-catheter and guidewire modules 3-DOF each (clamp, translate, rotate), balloon module 2-DOF (choi2021_vascular Sec. 2.1.2, p. 3)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (tightly pressed roller pairs, 20 mm rollers driven through bevel gears) (choi2021_vascular Sec. 2.1.1, p. 2-3)
robots.rotation_detail: Roller pair rubs the device: a motor, bevel gear and ball screw raise the cartridge frame; limited range of about 900-1800 degrees from a 25 mm vertical displacement (Sec. 2.3.2, p. 7); clamping by motor, timing belt and bidirectional ball screw (p. 4)
robots.device_range: accommodates instruments of various sizes via the active clamping mechanism; rotation range about 900-1800 degrees per cartridge stroke (p. 7); translation stroke and speeds N.R.
robots.force_sensing: none: no force sensor; the haptic cue is a virtual wall near the cartridge rotation limit, computed from cartridge position (choi2021_vascular Discussion, p. 17)
robots.haptics_leader: master: 3-RRR planar parallel mechanism + linear actuator ('clutch-like trigger') + spherical wrist mechanism, called a 6-DOF mechanism (Sec. 2.1.3, p. 4-5; p. 17), Maxon DC motors; force feedback used only as a virtual wall
robots.imaging_compat: real-time fluoroscopy on the console monitors; physician behind radiation-shielded glass (choi2021_vascular p. 5, Fig. 17b)
robots.sterility: roller cartridge designed as a disposable part (p. 4); sterile drapes and detachable sterilised rollers form the sterile interface, no closed housing (p. 15, 17)
robots.validation_detail: bench: 20 cartridge-gap trials, 10 repetitions per translation length and per 360-degree rotation; phantom: EVE silicone model, trial count N.R.; animal: one 60 kg pig, robot-driven guidewire into the RCA; clinical: 2 patients (coronary angiography), robot-driven guidewire to the LAD and the RCA, both technically successful; MFDS approval 20190064902 (choi2021_vascular p. 9-16)
robots.key_numbers: translation mean error: guiding catheter -0.93 to 0.75 mm, guidewire 0.11-0.86 mm, balloon 0.07-0.57 mm (Table 1); rotation error at 360 degrees: guiding catheter 3.29 +- 5.48, guidewire 1.93 +- 2.50 degrees (Table 2) (choi2021_vascular)

robots.n_dof_detail: 4 (2016: insertion and rotation of catheter and guidewire, cha2016_assembly p. 71); 7 (CRR: insertion and rotation of catheter, guidewire and micro-guidewire, insertion of microcatheter, kim2023_robotassisted p. 1566)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (2016 guidewire: active and passive roller, spring-adjusted friction) plus other: rack-and-pinion carriage that moves the catheter drive (cha2016_assembly p. 72); CRR drive type N.R. (kim2023_robotassisted)
robots.rotation_detail: 2016: plastic gear trains rotate the catheter (Y-connector fixed to the rotation part) and the guidewire roller unit (cha2016_assembly p. 72); CRR N.R.
robots.device_range: commercially available devices; 2016 catheter drive stroke 460 mm (cha2016_assembly p. 73); CRR 5 F catheter stroke 45 cm, microcatheter stroke 20 cm longer (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1568-1569)
robots.force_sensing: Guidewire-tip contact estimated from actuator current, no dedicated sensor: under 200 mA in a straight artery, +300 mA curved, +500 mA blocked (cha2016_assembly p. 76); CRR N.R.
robots.haptics_leader: 2016: 2-DOF parallel-mechanism master (insertion, rotation) with two DC motors for haptic feedback, activate/release and catheter/guidewire mode buttons (cha2016_assembly p. 74); CRR: finger-grip handle with activate/release buttons (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1566), force feedback N.R.
robots.imaging_compat: 2016: camera over a transparent water-filled phantom; CRR: hybrid angio-CT suite (Canon INFX-8000C with Aquilion), robot mounted on the angiotable (kim2023_robotassisted p. 1567, Fig. 2a)
robots.sterility: Device-contacting parts detach and are EtO-sterilised (all but the roller actuator part), assembly 86 s (cha2016_assembly p. 73, 77); the same for the CRR (kim2023_robotassisted citing cha2016)
robots.validation_detail: 2016: bench (10 insertion trials) and phantom (4 users x 3 trials; survey of 8) (cha2016_assembly); 2022: 2 swine as ECMIS advancer (hwang2022_ecmis); kim2023: single-centre prospective pilot, 10 HCC patients, 5 robot-assisted vs 5 conventional TACE, one operator; technical success 4/5 patients and 7/8 target vessels (one failure: 5 F catheter twisted in the telescope); no procedure-related adverse event
robots.key_numbers: 2016: max insertion error 0.63 mm, max response time 16 ms (cha2016_assembly). CRR: operator dose median 0.4 vs 53.2 uSv (P = .005); patient dose 2,167.5 vs 2,989.7 uSv (P = .311); procedure time median 56 (47-65) vs 37 (30-58) min (P = .101); 8 of 30 TACE steps robotised (abstract; Results: 8 of 22 procedural steps) (kim2023_robotassisted)

robots.translation_detail: other: concentric-tube drive at the tube bases rotates and telescopically extends three precurved superelastic tubes (Robotic catheter design)
robots.rotation_detail: concentric-tube drive rotates each tube at its base (Robotic catheter design)
robots.device_range: tube OD 1.875-2.77 mm; sensor: 8 mm silicone optical window with 2.5 mm working channel (Table 1; Haptic vision sensor design)
robots.force_sensing: no force sensor: tissue contact is inferred from the haptic-vision image (1 mm^3 NanEye CMOS camera + LED in an 8 mm silicone window); tip force set by the contact duty cycle (Fig. 1, Fig. 7)
robots.haptics_leader: Touch (3D Systems) six-DOF joystick for the teleoperated comparator; force feedback N.R. (Computer software design)
robots.imaging_compat: tip camera (haptic vision) for navigation; ultrasound monitor in the OR set-up (Fig. 2B); fluoroscopy N.R.
robots.sterility: drive system draped in plastic in the OR (Fig. 2B); valve and flush system at the inner tube's proximal end keeps air out of the lumen (Robotic catheter design)
robots.validation_detail: in vivo, Yorkshire swine 84.3 +- 4.7 kg with a custom leaky bioprosthetic aortic valve, transapical access: apex to annulus 5 animals / 90 autonomous trials (teleop 3 / 9, manual 3 / 13); circumnavigation 3 animals / 65 trials; to the leak 5 animals / 83 trials; occluder deployment 8/11 autonomous, 7/9 teleop, 11/13 manual (Results, In vivo experiments); ex vivo pressurized porcine heart for software testing (Fig. 5)
robots.key_numbers: autonomous 99% (89/90) apex to annulus; 95% (79/83) to leak; 66% (43/65) for annulus following; time 39+-17 s vs 34+-29 s teleop vs 31+-27 s manual; tip-to-leak distance 3.0 +- 2.0 mm (operator registration) and 2.9 +- 1.5 mm (autonomous) (Results)
robots.sim_model: none found (a data-replay simulator of recorded in vivo images and trajectories was used to develop the navigation software, Fig. 5; it is not a mechanics model of the robot)

robots.name: CorPath GRX
robots.full_name: CorPath 200 / CorPath GRX
robots.group: Corindus (Siemens Healthineers 2019-)
robots.versions: CorPath 200 (FDA 510(k) K120834, 2012-07-19; used in PRECISE, weisz2013_safety, and in the RAPID peripheral trial, mahmud2016_feasibility); CorPath GRX (K160121, 2016-10-27; PVI 2018; PMDA 2018; neuro CE/TGA 2019-2020); neuro cassette
robots.target_anatomy: coronary; peripheral; neurovascular (angiography, aneurysm coiling, carotid stenting; thrombectomy in vitro only)
robots.devices_driven: GRX: guide catheter (advance 100 mm + rotate), 0.014-in guidewire, rapid-exchange balloon/stent catheter; neuro cassette: microcatheter, 0.014-in wire, coils/stents (stent/stent-retriever compatibility limited); CorPath 200: all commercial 0.014-in guidewires, rapid-exchange balloons and stent delivery systems, guide catheter positioned by hand and connected to the disposable cassette (6 F in 119, 7 F in 45 PRECISE patients) (weisz2013_safety p. 1597-1598); RAPID: 0.014-in wires and RX balloons 3-7 x 20 mm, the over-the-wire self-expanding stent delivered by hand (mahmud2016_feasibility p. 2059)
robots.n_dof_detail: 5 for GRX (gao2026_legobot Table I via S8); CorPath 200: 3, insertion and rotation of the guidewire and insertion of the stent catheter (cha2016_assembly p. 70); li2024_design Table I says 2 (conflict)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller
robots.rotation_detail: clamped-wheel rotation of guidewire in single-use cassette (S8 csv)
robots.footprint_mm: N.R. (bedside arm on table rail + radiation-shielded cockpit)
robots.force_sensing: none (ren2023_critical Table IV); CorPath 200: proximal force measurement (rafiitari2014_current Table 3); no haptic feedback
robots.haptics_leader: no: CorPath 200 radiation-shielded mobile cockpit with console joysticks or touch-screen buttons (weisz2013_safety p. 1597), 2 joysticks (mahmud2016_feasibility p. 2059); GRX control console with touch screen and three joysticks for device, guidewire and guide catheter (Corindus media-kit image Control-Console_HR.jpg)
robots.imaging_compat: standard cath lab fluoroscopy; fluoroscopic, ECG and haemodynamic images slaved to duplicate monitors in the cockpit (weisz2013_safety p. 1597)
robots.sterility: single-use sterile cassette on the bedside arm (weisz2013_safety; mahmud2016_feasibility, cassette attached to the sheath with a Tuohy-Borst); drape not mentioned in these papers
robots.validation_detail: PRECISE 164 pts at 9 sites, 23 operators (CorPath 200, weisz2013_safety p. 1597); RAPID peripheral 20 pts/29 lesions, single centre (Graz), 3 operators (CorPath 200, mahmud2016_feasibility); GRX PCI 980 procedures pooled; neuro: 117-pt aneurysm study (10 sites), 214 diagnostic angiographies single centre, 6 aneurysm, 4 carotid stent, 10 angio/carotid; thrombectomy only in vitro/3D-printed models
robots.key_numbers: PRECISE: device technical success 162/164 (98.8%), clinical success 160/164 (97.6%), 2 conversions for stent-delivery resistance, procedure time 24.4 +- 14.1 min, fluoroscopy 11.1 +- 6.2 min, operator dose 95.2% lower in the cockpit than at the table (weisz2013_safety). RAPID: device technical success, safety and clinical procedural success 100%, 3 minor access-site haematomas, operator dose not measured (mahmud2016_feasibility). Neuro aneurysm: 110/117 (94.0%) without unplanned conversion, 117.3+-47.3 min total, 2 ruptures 2 strokes (mendespereira2024_evaluation abstract). Diagnostic cerebral angiography 214 robotic vs 636 manual: no difference in times or patient dose, conversion 39/214 (18%) (hamimi2026_learning abstract). Meta-analysis 7 neuro studies/265 pts: pooled technical success 87% (95% CI 75-96) (tan2026_corpathmeta abstract). Visceral: 16/18 (88.9%) technical success (wagenpfeil2026_visceral abstract). Automated movements on vs off 49 pts: conversion 22% vs 18% (ruggiero2026_evaluation).
robots.sim_model: none found (no public model of the robot; neuro in-vitro/3D-printed-phantom studies used the real robot: tomasello2024_modeling, kaneko2026_in, williams2025_robotic)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found; only fixed-rule automation in the product (Rotate-on-Retract, technIQ), alnooryani2018_rotate (human, 1 patient, full) - not learned; Siemens ARPA-H award 2026-08-20 aims at autonomous remote thrombectomy (press, not a result)

robots.name: ALLVAS
robots.full_name: ALLVAS (REIS)
robots.group: Aopeng Medical with Shanghai Changhai Hospital (Qingsheng Lu) and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Kundong Wang) (song2022_biomimetic affiliations; company not named there)
robots.versions: ALLVAS; predecessor: the group's first-generation robot ('similar to the first-generation surgical robot initially studied by our research group', song2022_biomimetic p. 14, refs 13-14 = Wang 2018 IJMRCAS 14:e1915 and Lu 2020 VES 54:598-604; not read) -> 2022 biomimetic system, 38 porcine cases (song2022_biomimetic; robot unnamed there, identified as ALLVAS by song2023_novel, which cites it) -> 2023 EVAR in patients (song2023_novel); 2022: Changhai (Q. Lu) remote-controlled robot driven by hollow ultrasonic motors, ex vivo phantom (Lu 2022) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 7 row 1, Fig. 13e; Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 QIN) (alekseeva2025_design; belikov2024_evolution)
robots.target_anatomy: aortic (EVAR), peripheral, coronary (one remote PCI)
robots.devices_driven: four manipulators with double V-grippers handle devices from a 0.014-in (0.36 mm) guidewire to a 40 mm stent-graft system (song2022_biomimetic p. 5); 2-3 devices at once in the porcine cases (catheter + guidewire, or stent-graft system, inner core and guidewire in TEVAR) (p. 10); up to 4 devices (song2023_novel); compatible with market devices
robots.n_dof_detail: 18 (slave: two three-axis arms and four manipulators, each manipulator with two DC motors and a stepper; song2022_biomimetic p. 4, 7); '12-DOF motion in the four directions of the short axis' (p. 14); 12 per mandhumula2025_robotic as REIS
robots.translation_detail: clamp-relay
robots.rotation_detail: rotatable V-grippers, continuous progressive rotation with relay gripper (song2023_novel)
robots.device_range: max axial speed 275 mm/s, min 5.15 mm/s, max thrust 27.45 N, max displacement 140 cm (song2022_biomimetic Table 1); rotation speeds 1.57 and 0.52 rad/s (p. 7)
robots.force_sensing: force feedback; force sensor on the manipulator (type N.R.), in vitro feedback delay < 60 ms, peak error 0.15 N (song2022_biomimetic p. 8); automatic mode halts above 2 N (liang2025_unleashing)
robots.haptics_leader: joysticks on a console outside the cath lab: button = clamp/release, knob = rotate, swing = advance/retract; force-feedback handle based on electromagnetic resistance (song2022_biomimetic p. 3, 7, 14; the paper says both 'four joysticks' and 'two sets of master joysticks')
robots.imaging_compat: mobile base, arm + manipulator
robots.sterility: detachable grippers, aimed at replacing all contact parts (song2022_biomimetic abstract, p. 14); single-use status N.R.
robots.validation_detail: EVAR 5 pts (song2023_novel); 4 pts programmed steps (liang2025_unleashing); 1 remote PCI 800 km (Xu 2024); animal: 10 domestic swine (45 kg), 38 robotic cases (PCI 8, TEVAR 4, renal stent 8, iliac stent 10, IVC filter 8), 5 surgeons, plus a 3D-printed aorto-iliac model (song2022_biomimetic p. 9-12)
robots.key_numbers: EVAR 5/5, operator dose -96.5% (song2023_novel abstract); remote PCI latency 30 ms, 800 km (chen2026_teleoperation Table I); swine: all technically successful, no adverse events, PCI operator dose 24.6 +- 2.72 uGy robotic vs 2224 +- 92.5 manual (the manual operator values equal the manual patient values in every column, possibly a table error), operative time not different, device exchange within 10 s, rotation accuracy 1 degree (song2022_biomimetic Table 2, p. 14)
robots.sim_model: yes for vessels/wire: SOFA-based training platform of Tongji group (yao2025_sim4endor, full); no model of the robot itself found
robots.sim2real_detail: YES: chen2026_learning (SAC + MPC filter, sim 49/50 -> phantom 18/20, full, IROS 2026); tian2026_visionlanguage (phantom 30/30, full); Tongji group lists 7 papers on ALLVAS/SOFA (S7b.md); liu2024_autonomous trained on robot not sim

robots.name: CGCI
robots.full_name: CGCI (Catheter Guidance Control and Imaging) remote magnetic navigation system
robots.group: Magnetecs Corp.
robots.versions: single system: animal validation in 10 pigs (gang2011_dynamically, abstract); initial human safety and feasibility protocol at La Paz University Hospital, Madrid, 5 flutter ablations (filgueirasrama2013_remote, Table 1); later discontinued (mandhumula2025_robotic: 'now seems to have been discontinued', 'not adopted commercially')
robots.target_anatomy: cardiac electrophysiology: right and left atrial flutter ablation (filgueirasrama2013_remote Table 1); pig left atrium mapping and RF lesions (gang2011_dynamically abstract)
robots.devices_driven: magnetized irrigated gold-tip EP ablation catheter (MedFact) with three permanent-magnet pellets at the tip, through an Agilis ES sheath (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1, Fig. 1); 4-mm-tip ablation catheter in pigs (gang2011_dynamically abstract); catheter 7 Fr / 2.2 mm (jeong2017_feasibility Introduction)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (mandhumula2025_robotic Table 1; alekseeva2025_design Table 14); field shaped by 8 coil-core electromagnets, push-pull by field gradient (filgueirasrama2013_remote Representative Results) plus a motorized linear catheter advancer
robots.translation_detail: magnetic (field-gradient push-pull at the tip); motorized linear catheter advancement mechanism with a sterilizable wheel-drive gearbox on a motor base, joystick-controlled slack/advance (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1, Fig. 2A, 2C)
robots.rotation_detail: tip direction by dynamically shaped field of 8 fixed electromagnets, 4 above and 4 below the patient in a semi-spherical chamber (li2020_magnetic Sec. 3.3; gang2011_dynamically abstract)
robots.footprint_mm: N.R. (semi-spherical chamber of 8 electromagnets around the torso, li2020_magnetic Fig. 5)
robots.force_sensing: none reported
robots.haptics_leader: no: right-hand 3D controller and left-hand 3-axis joystick at a remote operation console (filgueirasrama2013_remote Fig. 2B-C)
robots.imaging_compat: X-ray fluoroscopy, EnSite NavX electroanatomic mapping, EP recording and ICE unified at the operation console (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1); recording and fluoroscopic equipment unaffected by the fields (gang2011_dynamically abstract)
robots.sterility: sterilizable wheel-drive gearbox, disposable sheath clip and leg mount on the advancer (filgueirasrama2013_remote Fig. 2A)
robots.validation_detail: human: 5 atrial flutter ablations (3 left, 2 counterclockwise right), acute success 5/5, no procedure-derived complications, no recurrence at 3-11 months (filgueirasrama2013_remote Table 1); animal: 10 pigs, left-atrial mapping, linear and circumferential RF lesions, selective PV isolation in a subset (gang2011_dynamically abstract)
robots.key_numbers: field up to 0.16 T (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1); 0.14 T and 0.7 T/m gradients (mandhumula2025_robotic text); pigs, automated mode: 96 +/- 8.4% reproducible, 1.9 +/- 0.4 mm from target, 11.6 +/- 3.5 s to target, lesion depth 78.5 +/- 12.1% of atrial wall (gang2011_dynamically abstract); five initial experimental procedures: 95.7% reproducible, 1.9 +/- 0.9 mm, 23.28 +/- 14.8 s (filgueirasrama2013_remote Representative Results)

robots.group: Flux Robotics B.V. (University of Twente spin-off; Heunis, Misra)
robots.versions: Flux One: KUKA LBR iiwa with a liquid-cooled electromagnetic coil on a mobile trolley (heunis2023_flux Sec. II-B, Fig. 4); later system on a Doosan arm in the company photo (twente_fluxrobotics, article names 'Flux 2, the latest version'); described as a prototype of ARMM (utwente2023_flux; see armm_heunis2020)
robots.target_anatomy: fenestrated EVAR: coeliac artery and branches, SMA, left renal and contralateral common iliac arteries of an abdominal phantom (heunis2023_flux Sec. III-B)
robots.devices_driven: magnetic J-tip guidewire: Terumo Radifocus 0.032-in (0.81 mm) with a 10 mm tip of five NdFeB magnets, 2 mm diameter, silicone coated (heunis2023_flux Sec. III-A)
robots.n_dof_detail: 7 (arm and coil) + surgeon push-pull 1, guidewire bent in two planes (heunis2023_flux Sec. IV-C)
robots.translation_detail: magnetic (tip steering); insertion by the surgeon's hand at the bedside (heunis2023_flux Sec. I, IV-C)
robots.rotation_detail: coil pose (7-DoF arm) and coil current set field strength and direction (heunis2023_flux Sec. I-II)
robots.device_range: tip deflection -135 to 135 deg planned (heunis2023_flux Sec. II-A)
robots.force_sensing: none on the guidewire; arm keeps a 4 N virtual interaction-force constraint (heunis2023_flux Sec. III-A)
robots.haptics_leader: Omega.6 haptic device for coil positioning with force feedback at a virtual safety barrier, plus SpaceMouse, push buttons and touchscreen (heunis2023_flux Sec. II-B, Fig. 4e)
robots.imaging_compat: pre-operative cone-beam CT planning and live fluoroscopy in a hybrid OR (Siemens Artis Pheno); no CT artefacts per Siemens technician (heunis2023_flux Sec. III-B)
robots.validation_detail: silicone abdominal phantom from patient CT, 4 targets: one vascular surgeon with conventional (case 1) and magnetic (case 2) guidewire, 11 novice operators with Flux One; all targets reached, no adverse events (heunis2023_flux Sec. III-B, IV-A, IV-C). Company reports preclinical animal trials and first tests in Miami (twente_fluxrobotics), no published result
robots.key_numbers: coil field up to 60 mT (heunis2023_flux Sec. I, citing its ref. 18); guidewire navigation time -47%; target 4: 22.7 s vs 73 s (-69%); 11-37 s per target in case 2; mean SUS 80%; coil cooling 9.2 L/min keeps surface at 45 C; arm speed limit 0.02 m/s (heunis2023_flux Sec. III-IV)
robots.sim_model: virtual clone of the system for trajectory planning (Policy Improvement with Path Integrals), no guidewire physics simulator (heunis2023_flux Sec. II-C)

robots.name: COAST

robots.versions: 2020 3-tube design 0.40 mm OD (jeong2020_design); 2022 same family run under fluoroscopic path planning, ex vivo porcine aorta (ravigopal2022_fluoroscopic); 2023 larger 0.89 mm OD with 3-fibre FBG shape+force sensing (deaton2023_simultaneous); 2025 two-tube 'modified COAST', 0.35 mm outer tube, 0.66 mm Pebax sheath, joystick teleoperation (brumfiel2025_modified)

robots.devices_driven: the COAST wire itself (own nitinol-tube wire, not a commercial guidewire)

robots.rotation_detail: none in 2020 prototype; spur-gear roll of actuation module (2025)
robots.device_range: 2020 prototype 188-257 mm tubes, 'shorter than a clinical wire'; handheld spooling variant takes up to 1.5 m (chavenet2026_handheld)
robots.force_sensing: 2020: miniature force sensor on tendon tension; 2023: FBG triplet tip force, RMSE 0.005-0.027 N (bench)
robots.haptics_leader: no (Xbox controller teleoperation 2025)
robots.imaging_compat: fluoroscopy used 2022, 2025; MR compatibility N.R.
robots.validation_detail: ex vivo porcine aorta, navigation with COAST under fluoroscopic reconstruction (ravigopal2022 abstract); 2025: one qualitative teleoperated traversal of an aortic-bifurcation phantom with pulsatile flow, no success counts; 2020: phantom, no success count

robots.sim_model: analytical tendon-stroke / static model with experimental fit (jeong2020 Sec. III, full); shape-from-FBG reconstruction (deaton2023, full); no physics simulator found

robots.name: Hydraulic catheter
robots.full_name: Hydraulic steerable microcatheter tip (hyperelastic, saline-driven chambers)
robots.group: Friend lab, UC San Diego (Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering) with UCSD Neurosurgery, Radiology and Surgery; concept co-devised with Bernard Yan, Melbourne Brain Centre (gopesh2021_soft p. 1, 12)
robots.versions: Sci. Robotics 2021 (gopesh2021_soft); patent application US20190209811A1 'Hydraulically driven surgical apparatus'; Mooney-Rivlin constants in Gopesh and Friend, Soft Robot. 2020 (ref. 91); medRxiv preprint 2021.06.28.21258767
robots.target_anatomy: neuro: in vivo external carotid -> ascending pharyngeal -> parotid artery with coil deployment in the parotid artery (not intracranial); PCOM aneurysm coiling in a silicone phantom (gopesh2021_soft p. 6-9)
robots.devices_driven: own hydraulic microcatheter: 900 um outer diameter with four 50 um saline channels and a 400 um lumen, 15 mm steerable tip, 160 cm long Pebax shaft (gopesh2021_soft p. 3-5, 9); used through a 5 F guide with a 0.014-in Synchro2 micro-guidewire and AXIUM PRIME coils (p. 10)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3D tip orientation by pressurising one or more of four channels; no DOF count (gopesh2021_soft p. 1, 3)
robots.translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation (hydraulic: four saline channels bend the tip; insertion by hand)
robots.rotation_detail: none reported: bending direction set by which channel is pressurised; shaft rotation N.R.
robots.device_range: 160 cm; 180-degree bend (curvature 400 1/m) at 350 kPa, rupture at 1200 kPa (gopesh2021_soft p. 4)
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: no: handheld controller connected by microtubing (p. 9); in vivo a 1-ml syringe per channel locked with a one-way stopcock (p. 6); bench: Elveflow OB-1 pressure controller (p. 9)
robots.imaging_compat: fluoroscopic roadmap (Siemens Artis Zeego); gold radiopaque markers at three positions and barium-filled Pebax (gopesh2021_soft p. 5, 10)
robots.validation_detail: 2 Yucatan miniature pigs (47 kg), one per acute terminal session (gopesh2021_soft p. 11): navigation external carotid -> ascending pharyngeal -> parotid artery and coil deployment; patient-derived silicone phantoms (femoral to ICA; ICA to a PCOM aneurysm) with pulsatile flow, trial count N.R.
robots.key_numbers: 180-degree bend at 350 kPa, rupture at 1200 kPa (safety factor about 4); response time < 1 s through 1.6 m of 50 um tubing; length-to-diameter ratio 10,000:1; no endothelial injury or perforation on angiography (gopesh2021_soft p. 3-10)
robots.sim_model: ANSYS finite-element model of the tip (two-parameter Mooney-Rivlin) to choose channel radius and radial position; the channel count was fixed at four by the authors (gopesh2021_soft p. 4, 10)

robots.name: Magnetic soft wire
robots.full_name: MIT telerobotic magnetic soft guidewire system
robots.group: Zhao lab, MIT, with Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School (neurosurgery), University of Cincinnati and Philips Research North America; animal work under UMass Medical School IACUC (kim2022_telerobotic affiliations, p. 18)
robots.versions: 2019 ferromagnetic soft continuum robots: device only, magnet moved by hand and wire pushed by hand (kim2019_ferromagnetic); 2022 telerobotic system: KUKA arm with a 100 mm magnet, two motorised advancers, remote console, 400 um wire, pig (kim2022_telerobotic)
robots.target_anatomy: neuro (phantoms, porcine brachial artery with accentuated tortuosity)
robots.devices_driven: 2 devices, driven independently or simultaneously: own magnetic soft guidewire, 400 um OD (tapered nitinol core in a TPU jacket with 20 vol% NdFeB, magnetically responsive distal 50 mm, coreless 4 mm tip) and a microcatheter; 0.0115-in coils and a Solitaire X stent retriever delivered through it; 7 F sheath (kim2022_telerobotic p. 3-4, 18); 2019 prototypes 600 um (PDMS + NdFeB, 80 um nitinol core) and 810 um (TPU + NdFeB) (kim2019_ferromagnetic)
robots.n_dof_detail: 7-DOF arm (KUKA LBR Med 14 R820) sets the magnet pose (6-DOF end-effector control; pole flipped by turning axis 7 by 180 degrees) + 2 linear advancing units for wire and microcatheter (kim2022_telerobotic p. 3, 7, 17)
robots.translation_detail: magnetic (steering); insertion by two commercial worm-drive advancers (Stereotaxis QuikCAS Cardiodrive) driven by DC gearmotors through flexible shafts (kim2022_telerobotic p. 3, 18)
robots.rotation_detail: field direction, no shaft rotation
robots.device_range: magnet working distance d/R 2.64-3.67, i.e. 80-30 mT at the tip (kim2022_telerobotic p. 7)
robots.footprint_mm: N.R. (arm on a mobile platform beside the operating table, kim2022_telerobotic p. 3)
robots.mass_kg: magnet and fixture 7 kg (kim2022_telerobotic p. 18); arm N.R.
robots.force_sensing: none: 'the advancing unit of our system does not provide any tactile or haptic feedback' (kim2022_telerobotic p. 17)
robots.haptics_leader: no haptics: remote console a few metres away with a 6-DOF SpaceMouse Pro knob and buttons to advance/retract; ROS MoveIt/RViz virtual view (kim2022_telerobotic p. 17-18)
robots.imaging_compat: real-time fluoroscopy, DSA roadmaps, 3D rotational angiography; the NdFeB particles make the wire radiopaque; compatible with standard biplane fluoroscopy (kim2022_telerobotic p. 8, 17)
robots.validation_detail: head phantom under fluoroscopy (navigation 45.0 +- 4.0 s, n = 5); MCA aneurysm coiling and clot retrieval in phantoms (n = 3 each); 1 pig (56 kg Yorkshire, brachial-artery tortuosity model, 124.6 +- 19.7 s, n = 5); learning curve 6 novices and 2 experienced users x 15 trials; robot vs manual: one interventionalist, 10 trials each (kim2022_telerobotic pp. 8-16, 18)
robots.key_numbers: robot vs manual 42.9 +- 10.5 vs 63.7 +- 22.4 s (P < 0.05); the manual wire crossed the siphon aneurysm in 5 of 10 trials; field at most 80 mT, gradient 1.75 mT/mm; N52 cylindrical magnet 100 mm diameter x 100 mm; tip deflection about 120 deg (attraction) and 90 deg (repulsion) (kim2022_telerobotic pp. 5-16)
robots.sim_model: field maps in COMSOL; 2019 Abaqus finite-element model of the soft continuum robot (kim2019_ferromagnetic p. 13); MoveIt/RViz virtual scene used to plan magnet poses; magnet pose from joystick input via a Jacobian pseudo-inverse, no guidewire model in the loop (kim2022_telerobotic p. 17)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found (no learned controller in kim2019 or kim2022)

(cited as xu2023 ref. 36; not read); 2023 Adv. Intell. Syst. (Fu ... Du, Xu): UR10 arm carrying a D50 x L25 mm N52 magnet with a pole-flip stepper on a mobile cart, 4-DOF guidewire/catheter advancer, new tip, dipole + Cosserat models, trajectory planning, DSA test (xu2023_magnetically, full)
robots.target_anatomy: 2022: peripheral phantoms (silicone thigh vessels ID 1 mm to 1.6 cm); 2023: femoral artery -> aortic arch -> carotid -> intracranial arteries in a 959 mm silicone phantom (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 3.4)
robots.devices_driven: 2022: commercial hydrophilic guidewire (LWSTDA35150) joined to an Ecoflex + NdFeB (1:1 mass) soft actuator 2.5 cm long and 1.9 mm in diameter; 2023: 0.035-in (0.89 mm) commercial guidewire with two axially magnetised 0.5 x 2.5 mm N52 NdFeB magnets in a PDMS-filled silicone tube (0.5/1 mm ID/OD); the advancer takes 0.3-5 mm devices (guidewire and catheter), only the guidewire moved in the experiments (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 2.1)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2022: two symmetric gantries, each three linear motors (x, y, z) carrying a rectangular permanent magnet; 2023: 6-DOF UR10 arm + pole-flip stepper; guidewire and catheter advancers with 4 DOF in total (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 2.1)
robots.translation_detail: magnetic (steering); 2022 forward push by hand; 2023 advancer: stepper-driven friction-wheel pair with a spring/screw clamp (xu2023_magnetically p. 4, Fig. S1)
robots.rotation_detail: field direction; 2023 advancer rotates its linear module with a stepper and gear pair (xu2023_magnetically p. 4)
robots.device_range: 2023: advance speed 0-15 mm/s; magnet distance 40-180 mm (xu2023_magnetically p. 4, 8)
robots.footprint_mm: 2022 system 880 x 620 x 1600; workspace 700 x 500 x 500; 2023 mobile cart, dimensions N.R.
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: no; 2023 teleoperation console with an Xbox joystick through ROS (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 3.4)
robots.imaging_compat: camera in 2022 and on the 2023 bench; 2023 Philips Azurion 7M20 DSA in a cath room, system operated from outside the room (xu2023_magnetically p. 12-13)
robots.validation_detail: 2022: ring-passing task (8 mm rings) and path following, 3D vascular phantom; 2023: trajectory following in 3 resin phantoms (ID 10-13 mm, 160-180 mm long), teleoperated navigation to 4 intracranial targets in a 959 mm silicone phantom with pulsatile flow, one path under DSA in the partner hospital's cath room; repeat counts N.R.; pig tests named as future work (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 3)
robots.key_numbers: 2022: field 0-20 mT; deflection up to 180 degrees; localisation accuracy 8 mm (ring diameter). 2023: mean tip position error 1.52-1.88 mm and tip angle error 2.36-2.57 degrees over 3 phantoms; deflection up to about 100 degrees; navigation within 1-2 min; advance speeds 1.2-6.06 mm/s (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 3.3)
robots.sim_model: 2022 kinematic model; 2023 dipole field model, constant-curvature beam and Cosserat rod models (MATLAB bvp5c), COMSOL 5.6 field and tip FEM (xu2023_magnetically Sec. 2-3)

robots.force_sensing: N.R.

robots.full_name: Magnetically steerable PCI guidewire with a Helmholtz-coil EMA and a motorized feeding stage
robots.group: J.-O. Park, S. Park, C.-S. Kim, Chonnam National University and Korea Medical Microrobot Center
robots.versions: 2017: two pairs of Helmholtz coils + motorized feeding stage, feed-forward + PID steering (jeong2017_feasibility); 2019: EMA of two Helmholtz pairs and one Maxwell pair (one x-axis pair used) + linear-stage feeder, path regeneration, feeding control and vision tracking (kim2019_novel); 2018-21: same group's guide-wired helical microrobot (GHM) for mechanical atherectomy: 3D-printed corkscrew head (1.6 x 9.5 mm, NdFeB magnet magnetised across the axis) on a spherical joint at the tip of a 0.152 mm nitinol guidewire, steered by a uniform field and spun for drilling by a rotating field (18-370 Hz, resonant circuits) of three Helmholtz-coil pairs (30 mT), advanced and retracted by a motorised linear-stage feeder in an automatic tracing mode; in vitro feasibility (Nguyen 2018 EMBC); phantom path tracking, gelatin-thrombus drilling and 5 rats in vivo (Nguyen 2021 IEEE TBME 68:2490-2498, Secs. II-IV, Figs. 2, 4) (Konda 2025 Table 2 row 8) (nguyen2021_guidewired; konda2025_robotically)
robots.target_anatomy: coronary (PCI), tested in planar vessel phantoms; 2021: chronic total occlusion; rat abdominal aorta used as a coronary-size model (nguyen2021_guidewired Sec. IV-G)
robots.devices_driven: 2017: Asahi Conquest Pro 12 guidewire (tip OD 0.23 mm) with a bullet-shaped NdFeB magnet 1 mm x 7 mm (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 2.1); 2019: 0.2 mm nitinol wire with a magnet tip (kim2019_novel Sec. 4.1); 2021: 0.152 mm super-elastic nitinol guidewire (Confluent Medical) carrying the 3D-printed helical head; 130 mm of wire through a Tygon sheath (0.79 mm ID) as guiding catheter (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. II-A, IV-A)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2: insertion (feeder) + planar tip steering (field); 2021: insertion (feeder) + 3-D steering and spin of the head (field)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (motorized feeding stage with a guidewire holder, jeong2017_feasibility abstract; linear stage, kim2019_novel Fig. 1); tip steered magnetically
robots.rotation_detail: field direction of the Helmholtz coils (no shaft rotation); 2021: a rotating field spins the helical head on its spherical joint; the guidewire does not turn (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. II-A, III)
robots.footprint_mm: Helmholtz coil radius 162 mm, region of interest 100 x 100 (kim2019_novel Sec. 2.1)
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: no
robots.imaging_compat: overhead CCD camera only (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 3.1; kim2019_novel); 2021: optical camera on the phantom, C-arm X-ray (Ziehm Vision RFD) in the rat study (nguyen2021_guidewired Sec. IV-A)
robots.validation_detail: 2017: five-branch phantom (about 4 mm branches), insertion success 100% with feed-forward + PID vs about 75% with feed-forward only (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 3.3); 2019: smooth and sharply curved vessel phantoms, 3 paths x 3 replicates (kim2019_novel Sec. 4, Table 1); 2021: 5 rats in vivo (abdominal aorta, injected 9 % gelatin thrombus, contrast angiography): thrombus drilled without perforation in 3, blood flow restored in 2, rats 1 and 2 died during thrombus formation and rat 3 of bleeding after drilling; vessel phantom path tracking RMSE about 0.2 mm, maximum below 0.7 mm at 0.3 mm/s; gelatin thrombi in tubes drilled through, 54 mm (9 %) in about 48 s and 40 mm (11 %) in 43 s (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. IV-D to IV-G, Table II, Figs. 6-8)
robots.key_numbers: steering-angle error below 0.5 deg with PID vs about 7 deg feed-forward only (jeong2017_feasibility Sec. 3.2); tip-position RMSE 0.44 +/- 0.19 mm on path I, below 0.7 +/- 0.4 mm on all paths; feeding speed 1 mm/s; camera 0.1 mm per pixel (kim2019_novel Sec. 3-4); 2021: three Helmholtz pairs on three 15 kW supplies, 30 mT, rotating field up to 370 Hz; drilling force up to 0.8 N and torque 0.1125 mN m at 100 Hz; feedback steering error below 0.5 deg (maximum 0.52 deg) against about 3 deg feed-forward (nguyen2021_guidewired Secs. III, IV-A, IV-D)

robots.translation_detail: magnetic (tip steering); advance mechanism N.R. (lee2021_steering)
robots.rotation_detail: rotating field (20 mT, 12 Hz) spins the front magnet and drill tip for tunnelling (lee2021_steering Sec. IV-B)
robots.footprint_mm: cylindrical workspace up to 500 diameter (lee2021_steering Sec. II-B)

IV)
robots.key_numbers: steering at 20 mT; tunnelling at 20 mT, 12 Hz; stent release at 78.5 mT on average (theory 59 mT), 100% above 80 mT; stent position error 2.30 +/- 0.34 mm vs 8.79 +/- 0.69 mm for a conventional delivery catheter (lee2021_steering Sec. IV-B)

robots.name: Peristaltic catheter
robots.full_name: Peristaltically propelled active catheter: hydraulic two-balloon self-propelling catheter for the radial artery, driven by motorised syringes
robots.group: Nippon Institute of Technology, Department of Innovative Systems Engineering (Yuichi Nakazato, K. Takita, M. Higuchi; K. Kawanaka) (nakazato2017_peristaltic p. 79)
robots.versions: 2010: in-pipe micro mobile robot using peristalsis, hydraulic (nakazato2010_inpipe, J. Mech. Sci. Technol. 24:51-54; MAMM 2010), the mechanism the lab later tested 'using pseudoblood vessels with an inner diameter of <=6 mm ... assuming that the catheter is inserted in a femoral artery' (nakazato2017 Abstract; 2010 papers title only) -> 2016/2017: radial-artery catheter, section A 5 mm + section B 5/6/7 mm, phi 2.0 x 23.0 mm (nakazato2017_peristaltic Sec. 3.1, Figs. 2-3; MAMM-2016 proceedings, Springer 2017)
robots.target_anatomy: radial-artery access for coronary treatment (radial ID 2.0-3.5 mm, Abstract); tested in silicone tubes of ID 2.5 and 3.0 mm and in the right internal and external carotid arteries of an endovascular surgery simulator (EVE, FAIN-Biomedical) (Sec. 4.2, 5.2)
robots.devices_driven: its own active catheter, self-propelled: 'a self-propelled active catheter was realized without a guide wire' (Sec. 2); no off-the-shelf device
robots.n_dof_detail: 1: forward locomotion by a travelling wave of two alternately inflated sections A and B; no steering, no rotation (Sec. 2, Fig. 1)
robots.translation_detail: other: peristaltic self-propulsion inside the vessel: saline pressure-fed and aspirated alternately in balloon sections A and B, which grip the wall by friction and extend (Sec. 2, Fig. 1)
robots.rotation_detail: none
robots.device_range: catheter phi 2.0 mm x 23.0 mm, feeding pipe phi 0.4 mm (Fig. 3); balloon sections of silicone rubber OD 0.8 mm, wall 0.12 mm, joined by silicone tubes OD 0.4 / ID 0.3 mm (Sec. 3.1)
robots.footprint_mm: actuator: two syringe-and-linear-slider units in parallel, each 323.5 x 111.0 mm (Figs. 4-5 captions); connected to the catheter by a 1 m silicone tube (ID 0.5, OD 1.0 mm) (Sec. 3.2)
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: none (feed sequence of the two syringes; operator interface N.R.)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R. (photographed in a transparent simulator)
robots.validation_detail: phantom: forward driving over 30 mm in silicone tubes (ID 2.5 and 3.0 mm, Young's modulus 1.7 MPa, water-glycerin pseudo-blood 5.0 mPa s) at feeding rates 140-570 ul/s (Sec. 4.2-4.4, Table 1, Fig. 7); EVE simulator: moved forward in the right internal and external carotid arteries at radii of curvature up to 1.2 cm, moved backward at 0.8 cm (Sec. 5.3, Fig. 9). Number of runs N.R.
robots.key_numbers: max speed 4.79 mm/s at 570 ul/s and 370 ul feed (Sec. 4.4); design target 5 mm/s (Sec. 3.1); feed volume 230-400 ul (Sec. 4.3); catheter phi 2.0 x 23.0 mm (Fig. 3)

robots.name: MFCR
robots.full_name: MFCR: magnetic-controlled flexible continuum robot with C, J and S deformation modes, steered by a three-dimensional electromagnet platform
robots.group: Tsinghua University, State Key Laboratory of Tribology in Advanced Equipment (Zili Wang, Ding Weng, Zhaoxin Li, Lei Chen, Yuan Ma, Jiadao Wang) (wang2023_magnetic p. 1)
robots.versions: single version (wang2023_magnetic, Actuators 12:247, 2023)
robots.target_anatomy: coronary access through aorta-coronary bifurcations (PTCA-type guidewire navigation, Sec. 3.2); tested in 3D-printed ring channels (ID 4 mm, 30-130 deg), simplified aorta-left/right coronary models at three angles, and a Y-bifurcation with clay obstacles (Sec. 3.2-3.3, Figs. 5-6)
robots.devices_driven: its own magnetic soft continuum robot (guidewire-like): silicone elastomer with NdFeB powder (1:1 by mass) as the magnetic tip, nitinol-core silicone body (Sec. 2.2); advanced into the branch 'with the help of manual operation' (Sec. 3.2)
robots.n_dof_detail: tip deformation set by the field direction and strength (three planar modes C, J, S); insertion by hand (Sec. 3)
robots.translation_detail: magnetic (steering); forward push by hand ('with the help of manual operation', Sec. 3.2)
robots.rotation_detail: magnetic torque of the external field on the programmed magnetisation; no axial rotation (Sec. 2.1, 3.1)
robots.device_range: magnetic part L = 15 mm (segments 6, 3 and 6 mm with different magnetisation), D = 1.5 mm (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 3)
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: none (N.R.)
robots.imaging_compat: optical: DSLR camera, camera above the testbed (Fig. 1c, Sec. 3.1); fluoroscopy N.R.
robots.validation_detail: bench: static deformation in the three-dimensional electromagnet platform against the model, n = 3 per condition (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 4); phantom: passing 30-130 deg ring channels and aorta-coronary models with a permanent magnet (Fig. 5), and entering a branch past an obstacle with J and S modes in the electromagnet system (Fig. 6, Videos S1-S2)
robots.key_numbers: C-shape field 19.7-127 mT; < 150 mT in all tests (Sec. 4); max mean angle error 2.979 deg and max mean tip-position error 0.328 mm (Sec. 5); J mode 0.589 / 0.499 deg and 0.103 mm (Sec. 4); magnetised at 1.5 T for 10 s (Sec. 2.2)
robots.sim_model: yes: quasi-static model from magnetic plus elastic potential energy on an Euler-Bernoulli beam, solved in MATLAB to predict the deformation modes (wang2023_magnetic Sec. 2.1, 3.1)

robots.name: CASIA VasCure
robots.full_name: CASIA vascular robotic system: Dual-finger Robotic Hand (DRH) and VasCure two-channel PCI robot
robots.group: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA), State Key Lab of Management and Control for Complex Systems / Multimodal AI Systems (Zeng-Guang Hou, Xiao-Liang Xie, Xiao-Hu Zhou, Shi-Qi Liu, Gui-Bin Bian); animal tests at Shanghai Huadong Hospital
robots.versions: 2011 image-based guidewire navigation and delivery system (ji2011_guidewire, title); 2013 enhanced dual-finger robotic hand for catheter (bian2013_enhanced, title); 2015 dual-finger robotic hand (DRH): bionic thumb (driven roller, 2 DOF) and bionic forefinger (passive roller, 3 DOF); rotating the rollers about their axes advances the device, translating them in opposite directions along their axes rolls it; two steppers, guidewire gripper, console with handle and LCD panel; bench tests with EM tracking (feng2015_bioinspired, full: Sec. II-A, II-B, III); motion-scaling control (feng2015_motion abstract); 2020 Dual-finger Robotic Hand for Angioplasty, DRH: bionic thumb + bionic forefinger rollers on two steppers, DC-motor clamping, guidewire gripper (wei2020_novel Sec. 2, full); 2021 VasCure: one active + two passive rollers = two channels for two guidewires, graspers A/B, slave on a robot arm (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II, full) and 5G version with generalized predictive control (zhang2021_improved, abstract); 2023-2025 same platform in a white/blue housing on an arm used for learning-based delivery (li2024_modelbased Fig. 2; li2023_casog; li2023_discrete; wang2025_fuzzy); VasCure
robots.target_anatomy: coronary (PCI; bifurcation lesions with two-stent technique)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire (two guidewires in VasCure) and balloon/stent catheter; master has separate catheter and balloon joysticks; guide catheter advanced manually by the assistant in the pig test (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II-A, III-B)
robots.n_dof_detail: N.R. as a total; per channel guidewire translation + rotation (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II-B) 2015 DRH: thumb 2 DOF + forefinger 3 DOF (feng2015 Sec. II-A).
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller
robots.rotation_detail: other: active and passive rollers translate along their own axes to roll the wire like thumb and forefinger (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II-B); A4/chen2026 review calls it a subjacent lifting mechanism
robots.device_range: N.R. (DRH stated compatible with catheters and balloon/stent catheters of different diameters, wei2020_novel Sec. 2) 2015 tests: guidewire 0.35 mm (0.36 in Table I) and balloon/stent catheter 0.7 mm, displacement limited to 200 mm (feng2015 Sec. III-A, III-D).
robots.force_sensing: proximal: guidewire friction force from motor torque via a T21WN torque sensor (li2024_modelbased Sec. IV-B); no integrated force feedback in VasCure per chen2026_teleoperation (review) 2015 DRH: none; a torque sensor is future work (feng2015 Sec. IV).
robots.haptics_leader: no force feedback reported; master console = guidewire handle (push/pull + rotating knob), catheter joystick, balloon joystick, touchscreen GUI (zhao2021_vascure Fig. 3)
robots.imaging_compat: X-ray fluoroscopy (DSA in pig PCI); EM tracking used for bench accuracy
robots.validation_detail: Remote pig PCI over a 5G commercial network, surgeon about 10 km away, two guidewires to LCX and LAD then balloons along both (zhao2021_vascure Sec. III-B; one pig described); GPC controller PCI on an experimental pig, IAE reduced by at least 20% (zhang2021_improved, abstract); further 5G remote PCI pig trials reported by a review (Han 2023 via chen2026_teleoperation [57], review-level)
robots.key_numbers: VasCure max guidewire error 0.25 mm advance / 0.38 mm retract over 150 mm at 7.2-25.2 mm/s, 10 trials per speed per channel, EM tracker at 40 Hz (zhao2021_vascure Sec. III-A, Tables I-II); DRH mean axial RMSe 0.72 +/- 0.49 mm (wei2020_novel Abstract); review: 5G latency 90 -> 163 ms at 1100 km and 81 -> 161 ms at 18.3 km (chen2026_teleoperation, Han 2023); learning on the robot: CASOG 94.00 +/- 4.32% success (50 deliveries x 3 seeds; human demonstrations 39/42) on a 15 x 15 x 1 cm printed planar phantom (li2023_casog, arXiv HTML Table 2); CORVE 80.33 +/- 5.09% and 84.00 +/- 4.76% vs CASOG 69.67 +/- 2.69% on phantom 1 (li2024_modelbased Table II) 2015 DRH (feng2015 Sec. III): 5 trials per manipulation (guidewire and balloon/stent translation at 10 mm/s, guidewire rotation), speed sweeps 0.5-60 mm/s; RMS errors shown only as bar plots (Fig. 6), no number in the text.
robots.sim_model: group's own guidewire/vessel VR simulators (fast and stable guidewire simulator EMBC 2015; elastic guidewire simulator wang2018_simulator; titles only); no model of the robot found
robots.sim2real_detail: none found: the RL controllers (CASOG, CORVE, discrete SAC, offline-online RL) were trained on data recorded on the physical robot over a planar phantom with an overhead 140 x 140 px camera, not in simulation (li2024_modelbased Sec. III-A, full; li2023_casog Sec. IV, arXiv HTML); li2023_discrete (Robotica 2023, full): DSAC-AE learned guidewire delivery directly on the 2-DOF robot over a 15 x 15 x 1.5 cm 3D-printed planar model, 140 x 140 px overhead images, 10 discrete actions every 0.5 s, success after 50k real samples in < 15 h (Sec. 2.1, 4); the paper argues against training in simulation (Sec. 1)

robots.name: CASIA TTVR robot
robots.full_name: CASIA robotic transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) system
robots.group: Shuangyi Wang group, CASIA / University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and CAS Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, Hong Kong Institute of Science & Innovation, with Zeng-Guang Hou and Xiao-Hu Zhou; clinical partner Kent Chak-Yu So (CUHK, Prince of Wales Hospital)
robots.versions: 2024 TTVR system: passive stabilizer, robotic drive, detachable delivery catheter, valve manipulation mechanism; RL + Monte Carlo probabilistic maps + human-robot co-piloted control (wang2024_robotic, arXiv abstract); 2025 model-free delivery with Data-Enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) on the same drive and the LuX-Valve Plus delivery system, a camera standing in for fluoroscopy over a printed heart phantom (lin2025_modelfree, full); 2026 patient-specific geometry-aware planning + numerical-Jacobian IK control (lin2026_autonomous, abstract); 2026 virtual-physical simulation platform (lin2026_robotic, full)
robots.target_anatomy: right heart: tricuspid valve (transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement / intervention)
robots.devices_driven: large-bore steerable TTVR delivery catheter (detachable) with valve Delivery system: LuX-Valve Plus (Jenscare Biotechnology, Ningbo) (lin2025 Sec. II).
robots.n_dof_detail: 5 (overall forward/backward along the long axis, catheter rotation, outer-sheath advance/retract, bending of the bending tube, inner-core advance/retract; lin2025 Sec. II, Fig. 1(b)); 2 controlled (overall translation and bending; lin2025 Sec. III; lin2026_robotic Experimental setup)
robots.translation_detail: other: robotic drive of the delivery-catheter system; overall translation by its own motor, drawn as a pinion on a toothed rack in lin2025 Fig. 1(b) (the text does not describe the mechanism)
robots.rotation_detail: four motors in the drive unit, coupled through isolation parts to the instrument case that holds the delivery system (rotation, outer sheath, bending, inner core); "The power from the Drive Unit is transmitted to the catheter through the Isolation Parts without direct physical contact" (lin2025 Sec. II, Fig. 1(b))
robots.device_range: workspace drawn in lin2025 Fig. 1(c): overall translation -28 to 212 mm, rotation -180 to 180 deg, outer sheath -107 to 20 mm, bending -90 to 0 deg, inner core -20 to 20 mm (graphic only, not in the text)
robots.force_sensing: N.R.
robots.haptics_leader: leader side with operator interface and GUI (lin2026_robotic Fig. 2b); haptics N.R.
robots.imaging_compat: fluoroscopy (virtual fluoroscopy in the platform, 32 deg RAO / 7 deg CAU); optical shape/pose tracking of the catheter lin2025: a 640 x 480 px, 30 fps camera over the phantom stands in for fluoroscopy (Sec. IV-A).
robots.sterility: components above the isolation parts can be sterilised during surgery (lin2025 Sec. II: "the ability to sterilize the components above the Isolation Parts during surgery, while maintaining a sterile environment for the catheter")
robots.validation_detail: first-in-vivo animal study (species and number N.R. in the arXiv abstract; full text not read); 15 patient CT datasets + 3 cardiac phantoms with mm-scale tip tracking error (lin2026_autonomous abstract); 10 operators raw vs augmented virtual fluoroscopy and 10 closed-loop control trials on the virtual-physical platform (lin2026_robotic) lin2025: printed patient-CT heart phantom (SVC, RA, RV); 3 catheters x 3 random start positions and 3 camera poses x 3 runs (Sec. IV-A, IV-C, Tables I-II); still phantom level.
robots.key_numbers: co-piloted control better than master-slave in time efficiency, control efficiency, autonomy and stability (numbers N.R. in abstract); platform: tracking-to-CT registration 0.59 +/- 0.16 mm, landmark projection 2.31 +/- 0.60 px, input-to-display latency 255.6 +/- 13.4 ms, 2D angular error 15.02 -> 2.57 deg (median) with augmented fluoroscopy across 10 operators (lin2026_robotic Tables 1-2) lin2025 DeePC: "In most cases, the final error in slope is less than 1 deg and the error in intercept is under 3 pixels" for the tip line in the camera image (Sec. IV-C); worst case 2.55 +/- 0.04 deg and 3.37 +/- 0.17 px (camera pose 3, position 2, Table II); no success rate or time reported.
robots.sim_model: virtual-physical simulator: real robot-driven catheter, optical shape tracking, CT-derived virtual fluoroscopy in 3D Slicer 5.10 (lin2026_robotic)
robots.sim2real_detail: RL is part of the 2024 system (wang2024_robotic abstract); where it was trained is N.R. (arXiv PDF not read). lin2025_modelfree (full): DeePC uses a Hankel matrix of the operator's recorded master-slave motion and "does not require additional calibration or model training" (Sec. III-A, V); no simulator.

robots.name: Beihang VIR
robots.full_name: Beihang remote-controlled vascular interventional robot (VISR / VIR / RVIR / VIR-2) and its successor catheter operating robot (COR, 2016), the 2023 MIVI robot
robots.group: Beihang University Robotics Institute (Tianmiao Wang, Da Liu; 2010 corresponding author Dapeng Zhang) and Image Processing Centre / School of Astronautics (Cai Meng); clinical: Department of Neurosurgery, Navy General Hospital of PLA (Wang-sheng Lu, Zeng-min Tian; author affiliation in lu2011 and lu2016); 2023 version Beijing Institute of Petrochemical Technology (Shaoya Guan, Limei Ma) with Cai Meng
robots.versions: 2010 VISR: 5-DOF lockable passive hydraulic supporting arm + catheter navigator (rollers on a gear), PVDF tip sensor, Omega 6 master, glass model and 1 dog (wang2010_remote) -> 2011 VIR + virtual surgery training system, 10 beagles (lu2011_application) -> 2013 RVIR: image guidance (C-arm calibration, MicronTracker, catheter localisation, 3D reconstruction), Falcon master (meng2013_remote) -> VIR-2, 15 patients 2013 (lu2016_clinical, online 2015) -> 2016 COR, a new driver with bionic friction fingers, leadscrew rotation and a clamping motor, 2.6 kg, bench and glass model (meng2016_novel) -> 2023 MIVI robot with EM-tracked navigation (guan2023_multi; its Fig. 5(b) is the same photograph as meng2016 Fig. 5)
robots.target_anatomy: cerebral (angiography in patients); renal, cardiac chambers, cerebrovascular arteries in animals; aortic (2023 navigation: AAA, TAA, AD data)
robots.devices_driven: catheter only, one device: 1.5 mm catheters (wang2010_remote p. 200); 4F-6F (1.33-2.00 mm) single-bend catheters through a 6F sheath, guidewire not driven ('the medical robot controlled only the catheter', lu2011_application p. 363, 365); 5F single-curve catheter in patients (lu2016_clinical p. 133); COR: 4F catheter (meng2016_novel p. 307)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 active (axial: stepping motor 2; rotation: stepping motor 1) on a 5-DOF lockable passive hydraulic supporting arm (wang2010_remote p. 196); COR: translation, rotation and clamping motors (meng2016_novel p. 305)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (catheter clamped by rollers 1 and 2 driven by stepping motor 2, wang2010_remote p. 196; COR / 2023 MIVI: bionic friction fingers, meng2016_novel p. 305, guan2023_multi Fig. 5a)
robots.rotation_detail: the roller pair sits on a passive gear turned by stepping motor 1 through an active gear (wang2010_remote p. 196); COR: the two bionic fingers translate in opposite directions via a two-direction leadscrew and belt (finger rolling) (meng2016_novel p. 305); 2023: rotation motor (guan2023_multi Fig. 5a)
robots.device_range: catheter speed 10-25 mm/s (wang2010_remote p. 199; lu2011_application p. 364); stroke N.R.; COR 205 pulses per mm (meng2016_novel p. 307)
robots.mass_kg: COR 2.6 kg, aluminium alloy and steel (meng2016_novel p. 309); VIR N.R.
robots.force_sensing: PVDF piezoelectric film glued at the catheter tip, robot stalls above a threshold (wang2010_remote p. 198); lu2011 calls the force feedback virtual (p. 365); not used in the 15 patients (lu2016_clinical p. 136); COR none
robots.haptics_leader: Omega 6 haptic device (Force Dimension) (wang2010_remote p. 198); 3-DOF Novint Falcon in a shielded cabinet (meng2013_remote p. 231); master controlled over LAN, device N.R. (lu2016_clinical p. 133)
robots.imaging_compat: X-ray/DSA (GE LCV+ C-arm); RVIR image guidance with an H40 MicronTracker and C-arm calibration phantom (meng2013_remote p. 231-236); 2023: EM tracking + CTA-DSA 2D/3D registration
robots.validation_detail: 15 patients (March-September 2013), robot-assisted cerebral angiography, femoral sheath placed by hand, no complications (lu2016_clinical p. 133-134); 10 beagles (16-20 kg), 9 targets including both carotid and both vertebral arteries, 5 repeats, no complications (lu2011_application p. 363; meng2013_remote '10 dogs'); 1 dog, 5 targets, and glass model with 10 repeats per speed (wang2010_remote); COR: bench (10 trials per length 10-50 mm, 10 rotations) and glass model (meng2016_novel); 2023 vascular model only (guan2023_multi)
robots.key_numbers: remote positioning accuracy 1.05 +/- 0.28 mm; staff DSA exposure 0 min; procedure 25-41 min, mean 34.4 +/- 5.13 min (lu2016_clinical p. 134); catheter motion error < 0.5 mm in a glass model (wang2010_remote p. 199); distortion correction RMS 0.35 px, distance reconstruction RMS 0.53 mm (max 1.34 mm) (meng2013_remote); COR axial accuracy -0.04 to 0.34 mm, relative error within +-5% (meng2016_novel Table I); 2023: 2D/3D registration < 1 mm, EM positioning RMS < 1 mm and max < 2 mm over 4 paths x 26 points (guan2023_multi Results, Fig. 7)
robots.sim_model: virtual surgery training system (lu2011_application abstract); no controller-training model
