robots.name: HIT catheter robot
robots.full_name: HIT master-slave robotic catheter system for a steerable pull-wire catheter
robots.group: Harbin Institute of Technology, State Key Laboratory of Robotics and System (Yili Fu, Anzhu Gao, Hao Liu, Kai Li, Zhaoguang Liang) with Harbin Medical University
robots.versions: 2008-2010 active/steerable catheter navigation studies (Fu et al., IJMRCAS 2008-2009, titles); 2011 robotic catheter system (fu2011_development, full); 2011 master-slave catheterisation system (fu2011_masterslave, title)
robots.target_anatomy: thoracic/cardiac vessels (thorax vascular phantom, brachiocephalic trunk)
robots.devices_driven: custom 7 Fr single-curve pull-wire steerable catheter with two 5-DOF magnetic tracking sensors, two electrodes and a thermocouple (fu2011_development Sec. III)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (push/pull, rotate, bend; fu2011_development Sec. II-C)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller
robots.rotation_detail: other: both stepping motors at equal speed rotate the whole friction-wheel unit about the catheter (fu2011_development Sec. IV); bending by a lead-screw slide unit moving the handle sleeve
robots.force_sensing: proximal: two force-sensing elements between the inner and outer wheel of the active friction wheel (fu2011_development Fig. 6)
robots.haptics_leader: Novint Falcon 3-DOF handle with force feedback (fu2011_development Fig. 2)
robots.imaging_compat: EM magnetic tracking + MR-derived 3D guiding image (20 slices); intended to reduce X-ray use
robots.validation_detail: thorax vascular phantom (Shelley Medical), catheterisation to the brachiocephalic trunk (fu2011_development Sec. VI)
robots.key_numbers: image-sensor registration error mean 0.19 mm, RMS 0.49 mm, SD 0.46 mm over 700 wall points (fu2011_development Sec. VI, Fig. 9)

robots.name: SIA finger-twist robot
robots.full_name: SIA master-slave vascular interventional robot with bionic finger-twisting guidewire mechanism
robots.group: Shenyang Institute of Automation, CAS, State Key Laboratory of Robotics (Hao Liu, Tianyu Zhang, Peng Lin, Liming Zheng, Xiao He) with General Hospital of Northern Theater Command (Ximei Zhao, Jing Qiu); 2022 leader device with Shenyang Jianzhu University
robots.versions: 2022 master manipulator with force feedback (li2022_design, title/affiliations); 2025 slave with bionic finger twisting mechanism + force-based occlusion detection (zhang2025_obstruction, full); 2024: SIA (Hao Liu, Peng Lin) flexible-belt constrained catheterization robot: guidewire in a lumen of two magnet-joined belts pulled by friction rollers, rear-end clamp twists, bench delivery error <= 1.5 mm at 75-125 mm belt spacing (Tian 2024 ICMA; Alekseeva 2025 Table 10 row 4, Fig. 11e) (tian2024_flexbelt; alekseeva2025_design); 2017: SIA (A. Gao, H. Liu) with the General Hospital of Shenyang Command, contact-aided asymmetric tendon-driven ablation catheter (2.6 mm): tendons pulled by a motorised lead screw for the bench bending tests, left-atrium phantom reached by manual tendon, rotation and insertion (Gao 2017 RA-L) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 14 row 7) (gao2017_contactaided; alekseeva2025_design)
robots.target_anatomy: N.R. (vascular model with 4 branch regions)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire (twisted and advanced) and catheter (clamped by a solenoid valve) (zhang2025_obstruction Sec. IV-A)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 (axial delivery + rotation; displacement and rotation-angle mapping, zhang2025_obstruction Sec. III)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp
robots.rotation_detail: other: bionic finger twisting mechanism
robots.force_sensing: proximal: two force sensors on the twisting mechanism for axial force and radial torque (zhang2025_obstruction Sec. II-A)
robots.haptics_leader: master handle with two motors and high-precision encoders rendering axial force and radial torque (zhang2025_obstruction Sec. II-A)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.validation_detail: 40 interventions in a vascular model; occlusion detected in 36 (zhang2025_obstruction Sec. IV-B)
robots.key_numbers: occlusion detection 90% (36/40); axial force RMSE 414.15 mN; radial torque error 1.01 N·m as printed (torque traces are in mN·m); sampling 1 kHz (zhang2025_obstruction Abstract, Sec. IV-A)

robots.name: TJU linear-stepping
robots.full_name: Tianjin University linear-stepping endovascular robot with variable-stiffness SMP catheter and FBG tip-force sensing
robots.group: Tianjin University, Key Laboratory of Mechanism Theory and Equipment Design (Chengbin He, Shuxin Wang, Siyang Zuo)
robots.versions: single version (he2018_linear)
robots.target_anatomy: aortic arch phantom (ascending/descending aorta)
robots.devices_driven: custom catheter: shape-memory-polymer tube 2.5 mm OD / 1.0 mm ID with water cooling, silicone outer sheath 5 mm x 90 mm, four FBG fibres at the tip (he2018_linear Sec. Methods)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 (linear + rotation)
robots.translation_detail: clamp-relay
robots.rotation_detail: brushless DC servomotor (Faulhaber 1226S012B) turns the travel clutch on a gear pair through a conducting rotation ring (he2018_linear Sec. Linear stepping actuation unit)
robots.force_sensing: distal: four FBG sensors (0.16 mm) at the catheter tip with temperature compensation
robots.haptics_leader: no (PC user interface)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.validation_detail: vascular phantom insertion in rigid vs flexible state with tip-force monitoring (he2018_linear Fig. 11)
robots.key_numbers: two electromagnet clutches (front + travel); Faulhaber LM1247-100-11 linear motor, max 100 mm per step; insertion 10 mm/s in the phantom test; SMP Tg 35 deg C; rigid catheter holds its shape against a 1.8 N·cm load (he2018_linear Abstract, Sec. Methods/Results)

robots.name: XMU wire robot
robots.full_name: Xiamen University vascular interventional robot for sim-trained guidewire navigation
robots.group: Xiamen University (Yang Zhao, Ziyang Mei, Dezhi Wu, Gang Liu) with Shuxiang Guo (SUSTech / BIT)
robots.versions: 2024/2025 robot + Pymunk-trained RL agent (mei2025_transferring, full); same group and hardware table in FreezeSeg2RL (mei2025_freezeseg2rl) and EVEGARS (PRCV 2026, see A6 notes); 2020: Xiamen University (Y. Zhao) remote-controlled TACE robot with force sensing and bending feedback (Zhou, Mei, ... Zhao 2020, Micromachines 11:805) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 ZH2; Duan 2023 Table 1 row 13) (belikov2024_evolution; duan2023_progress; li2024_design; zhao2022_remote)
robots.target_anatomy: coronary paths (virtual tasks built from DSA images); transparent ex vivo vessel model in a water tank
robots.devices_driven: guidewire and microcatheter (mei2025_transferring Sec. IV-B)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 modules: guidewire delivery, guidewire rotation, microcatheter linear motion (mei2025_transferring Sec. IV-B)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller
robots.rotation_detail: other: rotating platform driven along the axis by the friction-wheel module (mei2025_transferring Sec. IV-B)
robots.force_sensing: none reported
robots.haptics_leader: none (discrete commands from agent or surgeon)
robots.imaging_compat: camera above a transparent model (no X-ray)
robots.validation_detail: transparent vessel model ('ex vivo vascular model'), 4 targets; RL agent 40 deliveries per target, interventional surgeon 20 per target, replayed expert sequence as control (mei2025_transferring Sec. IV-B, Table III)
robots.key_numbers: RL success 82.50 / 87.50 / 82.50 / 72.50% (targets A-D) vs surgeon 100% and expert-clone replay 0%; mean steps 41.61 / 36.8 / 45.94 / 54.10 vs 31 / 26.95 / 34.05 / 41.65; actions push/pull 10 mm, rotate 45 deg, wait 0.5 s (Tables II-III); simulation success 99.30 / 99.26 / 98.34% over three training stages (Sec. IV-A); HX8-U28 bus servos for friction wheels, ASM34AK steppers, ESP32 control
robots.sim_model: 2D Pymunk guidewire-vessel simulation built from DSA path reconstructions (mei2025_transferring Sec. III-A)
robots.sim2real_detail: yes, phantom level: agent trained only in 2D simulation and run zero-shot on the robot with camera images re-rendered to the simulator style (mei2025_transferring Sec. IV-B, full)

robots.name: Wearable VIR
robots.full_name: Yanshan University wearable vascular interventional surgical robot
robots.group: Yanshan University, Hebei Provincial Key Laboratory of Parallel Robot and Mechatronic System (Haoyang Yu, Hongbo Wang, Jianye Niu) with Fudan University Academy for Engineering & Technology
robots.versions: 2023 wearable system (yu2023_wearable; received 2023, IJMRCAS 2024;20(1):e2616); its fuzzy-PID position controller comes from the group's earlier robot Yu et al., Appl. Sci. 2021;11(2):611 (ref. 24, not read); the same group's 2023 complex-coronary robot is A2's yu_complexcoronary_2023; 2021: H. Yu / H. Wang (Yanshan) VIS robot with force feedback and flexible clamping (Yu 2021 Appl. Sci. 11:611) and precise-delivery VIS robot with an operating-sleeve leader (Wang 2021 IEEE Access), possibly one robot (Chen 2023 Figs. 6(d), 9(a); Duan 2023 Table 1 row 4) (chen2023_operating; duan2023_progress); 2018: H. Y. Yu / H. B. Wang (Yanshan) master-slave system: master with an operating sleeve that slides and turns on a shaft (ball and V-groove decoupling), two encoders and a magnetic-particle clutch for force feedback; wire feeder that clamps, pushes and twists the device with a fixed, a promoting and a rotating finger; five servo motors; bench: feedback torque of the clutch calibrated with weights from 0.05 to 1 N m, about linear in the clutch current (Yu 2018 RCAR, Secs. II, IV, Figs. 2, 6, 11); the group's 2011-2015 mechanisms (X. Yang, H. Wang; Zhao 2022 Table 1 row 8b, Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 YA) are earlier versions, not read (yu2018_master; zhao2022_remote; belikov2024_evolution)
robots.target_anatomy: coronary (PCI): radial artery to the coronary arteries in a human vessel model, femoral access to the right coronary artery in a pig (yu2023_wearable Sec. 2.3.3-2.3.4)
robots.devices_driven: one guidewire or one catheter at a time; catheter and guidewire cannot be driven together (Sec. 4). Animal study: Cordis ATW guidewire (ATW-595-ME014) through a manually placed MPA1 8F catheter (Sec. 2.3.4)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 device DOF: clamp, push/pull, twist (Sec. 2.1, Sec. 5); plus DM pitch set by a linear actuator and position on a lockable slideway of the wearable frame (Sec. 2.1.2, Fig. 6)
robots.translation_detail: clamp-relay: fixing module (F1, F2) holds the wire while the clamping module (C1, C2) on a screw-driven slider pushes, then they swap ('reciprocating delivery'; Sec. 2.1.2, Figs. 7-8); propulsion DC motor 26SYK55.24 (Sec. 2.2.1)
robots.rotation_detail: wedge-shaped gripper closed by a crank-rocker and spring, rotated with the clamped wire through a gear set by a Maxon RE13 motor (Sec. 2.1.2, Fig. 9)
robots.force_sensing: slave: pressure sensor (SBT674-10 N) under the clamping module, a lever with arm ratio l1/l2 = 3 amplifies the delivery resistance 3x (Sec. 2.1.2, Fig. 10); master: torque sensor (DSN-206) in the handle drive (Sec. 2.2.1)
robots.haptics_leader: custom 3-DOF handle (operating manipulator): slide and rotation read by encoders, three-button squeeze read by a thin-film sensor (Flexiforce) sets the clamp; a servo motor with torque sensor drags the handle, velocity-force mapping slows it as delivery resistance rises (Sec. 2.1.1, 2.2.2, Figs. 2-5, 14)
robots.imaging_compat: used under a C-arm angiography system in the pig study (Sec. 2.3.4, Fig. 19); radiolucency N.R.
robots.sterility: driven gear shaft and gripper held by a magnetic cover, removed and replaced after surgery for sterilisation (Sec. 2.1.2); drape N.R.
robots.validation_detail: bench: 5 push and 5 twist master-slave tracking runs, 5 force-feedback runs (Sec. 2.3.1-2.3.2); human vessel model: 4 untrained testers x 3 targets x 3 trials, all 12 target deliveries within 60 s by the 3rd trial (Table 1); animal: 1 Bama pig (SIAT), guidewire to the right coronary artery, 3 robotic vs 3 manual deliveries, delivery time +2.46 %, operator exposure time -71.50 % (Sec. 2.3.4, 3.4, Fig. 23)
robots.key_numbers: static error 0.048 mm (0.019 %), relative dynamic error 0.204 % over 250 mm; rotation static error 1.259 deg (0.682 %), relative dynamic 2.217 % over 400 deg; force-feedback error mean 0.021 N, max 0.055 N (mean 2.566 %, max 6.746 %) (Sec. 3.1-3.2); 5 motors in master + slave; wireless NRF24L01 master-slave link (Sec. 2.2.1)

robots.name: HKU MR-safe robot
robots.full_name: HKU MR-safe hydraulic robotic manipulator for MRI-guided intracardiac (EP) catheterization
robots.group: The University of Hong Kong, Department of Mechanical Engineering (Ka-Wai Kwok; Kit-Hang Lee, Ziyang Dong, Xiaomei Wang) with Imperial College London (Su-Lin Lee, Wayne Luk) and CUHK Prince of Wales Hospital (Alex P. W. Lee)
robots.versions: 2018 MR-safe hydraulic manipulator (lee2018_mr, full); 2018 model-based (constant-curvature) vs model-free (Jacobian estimated online from EM tip data, no training) teleoperation with a Novint Falcon leader, 10 participants (wang2018_experimental, full); 2019 high-performance continuous hydraulic motor (dong2019_highperformance, title); 2022 upgraded 3-DoF platform with three-cylinder hydraulic actuation units, multicore FBG shape sensing, MR tracking markers and a learning-based piecewise-constant-curvature model; 800 x 140 x 210 mm, insertion 0-340 mm (dong2022_shape, full)
robots.target_anatomy: cardiac electrophysiology: left atrium, pulmonary vein isolation
robots.devices_driven: standard clinical EP ablation catheter (about 1.5 m, diameter < 3 mm) 2022: Thermocool Bi-Directional EP catheter (Biosense Webster), 8 Fr, about 2.67 mm (dong2022 Sec. II-A, IV-A).
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 in lee2018 (steering/bending, rotation, coarse insertion, fine insertion; lee2018 Table I); 3 (bending, rotation, insertion) in wang2018 Fig. 1 and dong2022 Fig. 6 caption
robots.translation_detail: other: master-slave hydraulic rolling-diaphragm actuators; coarse insertion through a transmission belt, fine insertion stage 2022: rolling-diaphragm three-cylinder actuation units for rotation and insertion (dong2022 Sec. IV-A, Table I).
robots.rotation_detail: hydraulic rolling-diaphragm piston pair to gear (rotary) unit
robots.device_range: clinically used EP catheters held in modular 3D-printed holders (lee2018); 2022 ranges: bending -60 to 60 deg at the catheter tip, rotation -360 to 360 deg, insertion 0-340 mm (dong2022 Table I)
robots.footprint_mm: 780 x 105 x 210 (lee2018); 800 x 140 x 210 (2022 platform, dong2022 Table I)
robots.force_sensing: none on the catheter; hydraulic force-transmission efficiency estimated 70%
robots.haptics_leader: Novint Falcon 3D haptic device with a Unity virtual endoscopic view (wang2018 Sec. "Robot control interface"); 2022: hydraulic master units driven by motors in the control room, no haptic leader described (dong2022 Sec. IV-A)
robots.imaging_compat: MR safe: 1.5 T GE SIGNA, SNR loss < 2%, no artefacts; active MR tracking coils on the catheter 2022: tested in a 1.5 T GE SIGNA; 10 m nylon pipelines at 0.1 MPa (dong2022 Sec. V-G, Table I); MR tracking markers about 0.48 mm (Sec. II-C); the tip electrode causes an image artefact (Sec. V-G).
robots.validation_detail: LA phantom ablation task, 127 targets (lee2018_mr Fig. 8); 10 subjects, model-based vs model-free in random order, 121 target spheres around the pulmonary vein ostium in a soft printed LA phantom (wang2018 Sec. "Simulated ablation task"); 2022: pulmonary vein isolation on a slice of swine tissue in a silicone LA phantom with pulsatile flow, 12 of 15 targets reached (80.0 %) (dong2022 Sec. V-B to V-F); in the 1.5 T scanner, marker tracking and feedback control with the LA phantom in a water container, no ablation reported in the scanner (dong2022 Sec. V-G)
robots.key_numbers: ranges: steering +/-45 deg (0.063 deg), rotation +/-360 deg (0.504 deg), coarse 0-200 mm (0.115 mm), fine 0-30 mm (0.016 mm); about 10 m nylon pipelines 6/4 mm, distilled water <= 0.3 MPa; hysteresis 0.88-1.29 mm for 0.05-0.2 MPa preload; delay 45-66 ms at 15 Hz (lee2018_mr Table I, Sec. III); model-free vs model-based (10 subjects): tip-to-target distance 5.61 vs 6.94 mm (19.1 %, p = 0.08), missed targets 33.3 vs 51.9 % (35.8 %, p = 0.03), maximum continuously missed targets 46.2 % fewer (p = 0.01) (wang2018 Table 1); 2022: shape error 2.33 deg per FBG segment; position error 0.63 mm over 21 segments and 1.53 mm at the tip (max 2.27 mm); path following 0.62 mm mean (2.34 mm max) with the learning-based model vs 1.07 mm (4.27 mm) analytical; autonomous targeting 16.9 s per target (dong2022 Sec. V-A, V-B, V-D, V-E)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found (wang2018: the model-free controller updates its Jacobian online from EM data; dong2022: the network is trained on FBG data of the real catheter, Sec. III-B)

robots.name: Nagoya robot
robots.full_name: Nagoya University catheter-driving robots for intravascular neurosurgery (roller and linear-stepping drives) with the EVE patient-specific simulator
robots.group: Nagoya University (Toshio Fukuda, Fumihito Arai; neurosurgeon Makoto Negoro), later Seiichi Ikeda and Carlos Tercero
robots.versions: 1996 ICRA networked telesurgery over optical fibre (arai1996_multimedia, doi:10.1109/ROBOT.1996.503883, title via dblp; cited as ref. 1 of tanimoto2000); 2000 MICCAI telesurgery system (tanimoto2000_telesurgery, full): 2-DOF roller slave whose outer shell turns for rotation, inner unit hung on strain-gauge beams (2-axis force), slave 'first designed in 1994' (Fig. 3), wire-driven 2-DOF master joystick (1.6 um, 0.023 deg encoders), 1.2 x 5 mm tip micro force sensor (0.5 mN, 2 kHz), in vitro telesurgery in an intravascular operating room with the doctor 5 m away watching X-ray (Sec. 3, 5); 2001 robotic controlled catheter system with motorized roller feeding (Negoro et al., via miyachi2025_robotics Fig. 1 and text); 2002 linear-stepping slave ('mechanical pencil' mechanism): two grasping units knocked by voice-coil motors, DC-motor rotation of the grasped catheter, voice-coil brake, disposable grasping unit, tip micro force sensor and force-feedback master joystick designed (arai2002_new, full; it replaces the 2000 roller slave, which slipped and was hard to sterilise); 2006 patient-specific neurovascular simulator EVE for evaluating robots (ikeda2006_patientspecific, title); 2007 IJMRCAS autonomous catheter insertion with magnetic motion capture (tercero2007_autonomous, full): the 2002 linear-stepping mechanism rebuilt as a stand-alone unit with a microcontroller, 2 DOF (insert/extract at variable speed, twist in one direction), steered by an NDI Aurora 0.8 x 8 mm coil (Sec. Catheter insertion mechanism, Fig. 2a); 2010 catheter insertion robot with photoelastic stress visualisation (ikeda2010_threedimensional, title)
robots.target_anatomy: cerebral (intravascular neurosurgery)
robots.devices_driven: catheter (4 Fr, 1.35 mm, in the 2002 tests; arai2002 Sec. 3)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 (forward/backward and rotation) for the 2002 slave (arai2002 Sec. 2.1)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (2000-2001 roller feeding; arai2002 Sec. 1: when the vessel's resistance exceeds the pushing force, the roller slips); 2002 linear-stepping slave: two grasping units knocked by voice-coil motors, a brake holds the catheter between strokes (clamp-relay type; arai2002 Sec. 2.2)
robots.rotation_detail: 2002: a DC motor (Table 1: 12 V, gear ratio 22:1) turns the grasping unit while it holds the catheter (arai2002 Sec. 2.2)
robots.device_range: 4 Fr catheter in the tests; step per cycle settable from 1 to 10 mm (arai2002 Sec. 3)
robots.footprint_mm: 2002 slave about 300 mm long (arai2002 Sec. 2.3: "about 30cm"); other dimensions N.R.
robots.force_sensing: 2002: a micro force sensor at the catheter tip measures the catheter-vessel contact force for force feedback and the brake (arai2002 Sec. 2.3; no force data reported); none in the drive itself (he2018_linear Introduction); photoelastic stress in the phantom used to visualise wall stress (2010, title); 2000 roller slave: strain gauges on thin beams measure push and rotation reaction forces, plus a 1.2 mm x 5 mm tip micro force sensor (resolution 0.5 mN, 2 kHz) displayed together on the master (tanimoto2000 Sec. 3.2-4.1)
robots.haptics_leader: 2002: master joystick with force feedback designed (arai2002 Sec. 2.3, Fig. 10); not evaluated; 2000: 2-DOF force-reflecting master joystick (prismatic + revolute, wire-driven, no gears) with variable-impedance and multi-sensor force display (tanimoto2000 Sec. 3.1, 4)
robots.imaging_compat: 2000: in vitro telesurgery under the X-ray camera of an intravascular operating room, master in the next room (tanimoto2000 Sec. 5, Fig. 11); 2007: NDI Aurora magnetic motion capture (tercero2007)
robots.sterility: 2002: disposable grasping unit and brake contact part (arai2002 Sec. 2.1, 2.2); the earlier roller slave was not suitable for sterilisation (arai2002 Sec. 1)
robots.validation_detail: in vitro patient-specific membranous silicone cerebral artery models (EVE) (ikeda2006_patientspecific, title-level); clinical use N.R.; 2001 system 'quite large', forward/backward only, not practical (miyachi2025_robotics) 2002 slave: bench only, catheter driven forward, backward and in rotation with the tip in a 5 mm pipe, distance by optical encoder (arai2002 Sec. 3, Figs. 12-18). 2000: in vitro telesurgery, soft plastic tube vessel model under X-ray in the intravascular operating room (tanimoto2000 Sec. 5). 2007: autonomous insertion in silicone block and membranous models of the aortic arch and carotids, speed control and 1-D / 2-D path reconstruction (tercero2007).
robots.key_numbers: 2002 slave: brake holding force about 220 gf, adjustable 0-300 gf (arai2002 Sec. 2.2); with the step set to 1 mm the measured step was 0.3-1.9 mm, so the stroke was "not stable" (Sec. 4, Fig. 18); slower than a roller drive (Sec. 2.1). Other papers not read. 2007: catheter speed controlled at 6.14 mm/s; 2-D path reproduced with < 7 mm error (tercero2007 Abstract).
robots.sim_model: physical in vitro simulator (EVE), not a computational model; EVE phantoms are reused by later robot studies (e.g. A2 southeast_jin2024)

robots.name: Aichi support robot
robots.full_name: Neuroendovascular intervention support robot with insertion-force sensing (Aichi)
robots.group: Aichi Medical University, Department of Neurosurgery and Neuroendovascular Therapy Center (Shigeru Miyachi) with Aichi University of Technology (Yoshitaka Nagano) and Nagoya City University (T. Hironaka) (miyachi2019_novel affiliations)
robots.versions: 2019 prototype with 2 independent slaves and 2-joystick master (miyachi2019_novel, World Neurosurg 127:e617, full); 2021 remote operation over LAN (miyachi2021_remote, PMC HTML); 2025 review with miniaturised 3D-printed slave and automatic coil insertion (miyachi2025_robotics)
robots.target_anatomy: cerebral (aneurysm coiling)
robots.devices_driven: microcatheter (forward/back) and microguidewire (forward/back/twist) at once, by two independent slaves; guiding catheter placed manually (miyachi2019_novel Methods, Fig. 3); coil delivery in the 2025 version (miyachi2025_robotics Fig. 3)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (MC translation; MGW translation + rotation) (miyachi2019_novel Slave Manipulator, Fig. 3)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller: device pinched between two rollers, DC motor through a 523:1 gear, upper roller in an open-close cover; roller grip set to slip above 1 N push (miyachi2019_novel Slave Manipulator, Driving Speed and Safety Function)
robots.rotation_detail: MGW roller unit and force sensor sit inside a drum turned by an engaging roller with a rubber anti-slip belt; battery inside the drum allows 360 deg rotation (miyachi2019_novel Slave Manipulator, Fig. 3); Bluetooth link to its motor in 2021 (miyachi2021_remote)
robots.force_sensing: proximal: push/pull force sensor behind the MGW roller actuator, shown on the monitor in newtons and as a musical tone; repeatability +/-0.04 N (miyachi2019_novel Slave Manipulator, Results, Figs. 4-5); insertion-force sensor in the Y-connector in later versions
robots.haptics_leader: no haptics; two joysticks (left MC, right MGW; tilt left/right advances/withdraws, forward/back twists the MGW, speed proportional to tilt) with audio/visual force display (miyachi2019_novel Master Manipulator)
robots.imaging_compat: X-ray angiography room: clinical simulation on the aneurysm model in a standard AngioSuite with the operator in the control room (miyachi2019_novel Fig. 7)
robots.sterility: slave units are waterproof; electric cords and circuit boards under the supporting frame (miyachi2019_novel Slave design); drape N.R.
robots.validation_detail: bench: > 50 master-slave trials without error motion, force-gauge calibration (miyachi2019_novel Results); phantom: microcatheterisation and aneurysm-sac insertion in a wet EVE silicone whole-vessel model with closed saline circulation under fluoroscopy, repeated AngioSuite trials all successful (Results, Figs. 6-7); remote coiling with the master 50 m away over LAN/HTTP (miyachi2021_remote)
robots.key_numbers: slave output force > 1 N; guidewire speed about 1 mm/s (523:1 gear); slave roller slips above 1 N pushing load (safety); force gauge +/-0.04 N; start-motion lag 0.1-0.2 s (miyachi2019_novel); delays about 0.1 s each for motor stop, Bluetooth, video and network (miyachi2021_remote)

robots.name: KU force-reflecting
robots.full_name: Korea University force-reflecting robotic platform for cardiac (EP) catheter navigation
robots.group: Korea University, Korea Artificial Organ Center (Jun Woo Park, Jaesoon Choi, Kyung Sun) with Hui-Nam Pak (Yonsei University Health System) and Jung Chan Lee (Seoul National University) (park2010_development affiliations)
robots.versions: 2010 platform (park2010_development, Artif. Organs 34(11), full); 2011 forbidden-region haptic virtual fixture on the same master-slave platform, in vitro phantom (park2011_haptic, Artif. Organs 35(11), full)
robots.target_anatomy: cardiac electrophysiology
robots.devices_driven: one conventional cardiac ablation catheter loaded with its handle (park2010 Methods); 2011: 7 Fr Blazer II HTD EP catheter (Boston Scientific) (park2011 Methods)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (forward/backward translation, roll, tip-bending knob) (park2010 Methods, Fig. 1a); master 5 DOF (the 3 plus pitch and yaw for haptic rendering, Fig. 1b)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp: the whole catheter compartment (handle with roll and knob joints) rides a linear guide and ball screw driven by a Maxon EC-Max30 brushless motor; resolution 0.002 mm (park2010 Methods)
robots.rotation_detail: roll joint (Maxon EC16) turns the mounted catheter and knob joint as one unit (0.037 deg resolution); knob joint: coupling socket on the bending knob driven by an EC16 and a worm drive (0.00185 deg) (park2010 Methods)
robots.force_sensing: load cell (Dacell UMM-1kgf) between the translation joint and the catheter compartment on a sliding bearing measures the axial reaction force, 0.019 N resolution (park2010 Methods, Results); force can also be estimated from motor current (Abstract)
robots.haptics_leader: custom 5-DOF haptic master with a catheter-handle-shaped housing: knob read by a magnetic encoder (no force feedback), roll with encoder + Maxon RE13 for feedback, translation on a wire-pulley bar with EC-Max13, plus pitch and yaw; RTLinux-Pro hosts linked by Ethernet, 1 kHz force loop (park2010 Methods); 2011: image-based forbidden-region virtual fixture rendered at the master (park2011)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R. for X-ray; 2011 in vitro tests used a camera (Canon EOS 500D, 1080p, 20 fps, 0.37 mm/pixel) as a fluoroscopy stand-in (park2011 Methods)
robots.validation_detail: bench: master/slave synchronisation with step, sinusoidal and manual motion, force-sensor check against a push-pull gauge (park2010 Results); phantom: the catheter inserted by teleoperation into a 600 x 400 mm vessel phantom with human-like inner radii while the virtual fixture warned of wall approach (park2011 Methods, Results); animal tests planned (park2010)
robots.key_numbers: translation max 1000 mm/s and 83,000 mm/s^2, roll max 138 rad/s and 7,610 rad/s^2 (above the 300-700 mm/s and 11-43 rad/s required); force peaks 0.5 and 0.7 N detected, resolution 0.019 N; joint resolutions 0.002 mm / 0.037 deg / 0.00185 deg; 1 kHz synchronisation loop (park2010 Results, Methods)

robots.versions: single prototype (Prod. Eng. Res. Devel. 7:81-90; online 20 Nov 2012, issue dated 2013)

robots.name: EVAR platform
robots.full_name: INSA Lyon / Ampère low-cost robotic platform for endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR): two stacked conveyors pinch the guidewire, an X-Y table rolls it, simulation-driven haptic leader
robots.group: Laboratoire Ampère (UMR CNRS 5005), Université de Lyon, INSA Lyon (Iris Naudin, Minh Tu Pham, Richard Moreau, Arnaud Lelevé) (naudin2019_evar, affiliation line)
robots.versions: single version (naudin2019_evar, AIM 2019); its finite-element model of guide insertion comes from the INSA thesis of G. Mouktadiri 2012 and Mouktadiri et al., J. Biomed. Sci. Eng. 2013 (refs 5-6, not read)
robots.target_anatomy: abdominal aorta and iliac arteries (EVAR of an abdominal aortic aneurysm); patient-specific silicone phantom printed by additive manufacturing, spring-suspended in a water tank (Sec. II, III-A, Fig. 6)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire ("guide"); "it is also possible to drive a catheter by this system instead of a guide wire"; one device at a time (Sec. III-A)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 device DOF (translation along z, rotation about z) plus a prismatic gap adjustment (y) that sets the conveyor spacing for the device diameter (Sec. III-A, Fig. 3)
robots.translation_detail: belt/track: two conveyors placed one over the other pinch the guidewire, each driven by a DC motor, coupled so they turn in opposite directions (Sec. III-A, IV-A, Figs. 3-4)
robots.rotation_detail: other: an X-Y table translates one conveyor over the other, rolling the pinched wire about its own axis (cylindrical joint S1-S2; Sec. III-A, Figs. 3, 5)
robots.device_range: N.R. (conveyor gap adjustable "to use guide wires with different diameters", Sec. III-A)
robots.force_sensing: none on the robot; the force sent to the leader is the guide-aorta contact force of an ABAQUS simulation, looked up by inserted length (Sec. III-C, IV-B); the authors state it is not the force at the tool (Sec. V)
robots.haptics_leader: Geomagic Touch (6 DOF, 3 motorised); pressing a stylus button acts as pinching the guide (clutch), stylus translation and rotation are sent to the conveyors and the X-Y table; renders the simulated contact force opposite to the push (Sec. III-A, III-C, Fig. 7)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R. (no fluoroscopy in the platform; phantom in a transparent water tank)
robots.validation_detail: bench: conveyor translation tracking of the stylus reference trajectory with a proportional speed loop (Simulink/ControlDesk, Fig. 14) and recording of the rotation reference (Sec. IV-A); haptic lookup coupled to the platform (Sec. IV-B). The silicone aorta phantom is built for guide insertion but no insertion result is reported; real-time control was not achieved with MATLAB/Simulink/dSPACE and was re-written in C afterwards (Sec. V). Alekseeva 2025 Table 4 lists it as TRL3 (ex vivo phantom).
robots.key_numbers: motor speed command 0-10 V, direction 0/5 V (Sec. IV-A); simulated insertion speed 20 mm/s (Sec. IV-B); exit of contact for an arbitrary 90 deg rotation (Sec. V); tracking error shown only as a curve x10 (Fig. 14), no number reported (N.R.)
robots.sim_model: yes: ABAQUS finite-element model of the guide inserted in a patient aorta and iliac model (elastic, hyperelastic and linear composite materials; Mouktadiri 2013, ref 6) gives contact forces per inserted length, used as the haptic lookup table (naudin2019_evar Sec. III-B, IV-B, Fig. 8)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found (the simulation feeds an offline force lookup; no simulation-trained controller)

robots.name: UJN catheter drive
robots.full_name: University of Jinan compact continuous-delivery catheter drive with friction wheels in a disposable surgical box and a constant-force clamp
robots.group: School of Mechanical Engineering, University of Jinan (Tianxiao Cao, Rongyu Ge [corresponding], Yi Zhang, Wenlong Wang) (cao2024_cathdrive, affiliation lines)
robots.versions: single version (cao2024_cathdrive, IDITR 2024); Alekseeva 2025 Table 10 lists a design by the same authors (W. Wang et al. 2024, clamping bracket block) as TRL2 concept, not catalogued
robots.target_anatomy: N.R. (general vascular intervention; coronary, brain, liver and kidney lesions named in the introduction)
robots.devices_driven: one catheter (Sec. II); tests with a catheter (Figs. 13-14)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 (axial feed, circumferential rotation) (Sec. II)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller: two active and two driven grooved friction wheels in a disposable box, the active ones driven through three gear shafts by one motor; the box couples to the power unit by a triangular-prism shaft (Sec. II-A1, II-B, Figs. 2, 4, 7)
robots.rotation_detail: gear pair rotates the whole axial-feed unit, the feed motor rides along, wires through a conductive slip ring (Sec. II-A2, Fig. 3)
robots.device_range: N.R. (constant-force clamp adjustable by spring pre-compression, Sec. II-B, III)
robots.force_sensing: none (a sawtooth constant-force clamp caps the clamping force mechanically, Sec. II-B, III)
robots.haptics_leader: a "master manipulator" box stands on the bench in the platform photo (Fig. 12); its design is N.R.; the tests were run from upper-computer software (Sec. V)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.sterility: disposable surgical box holds every part that touches the catheter; reusable power unit below (Sec. II-B, Fig. 5)
robots.validation_detail: bench: 10 axial moves of 100 mm measured with a vernier caliper and 10 rotations of 60 deg measured with a protractor on the experimental platform (Sec. V, Figs. 12-14); no phantom. Alekseeva 2025 Table 9 lists it as TRL3 (ex vivo phantom).
robots.key_numbers: axial error -0.65 to +0.62 mm per 100 mm move; rotation error -2 to +2 deg per 60 deg (Sec. V); calculated: 19.72 mm per feed-motor turn, max feed speed 3845.39 mm/s, 0.05 rad per rotation-motor turn, max rotation speed printed as 6.42 rad/s in Eq. 11 and 6.24 rad/s in the text (Sec. IV); friction wheel radius 14.5 mm; feed motor 11,700 rpm with reducer 4.62; rotation motor 7,600 rpm with reducer 62.01 and gear ratio 2:1 (Sec. IV)

robots.name: BUPT guidewire robot
robots.full_name: BUPT guidewire feeding robot (friction-wheel push-pull, gear rotation) used for deep-RL guidewire feeding on a vessel phantom
robots.group: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, School of Automation (Deai Yang, Jingzhou Song, Yuhang Hu) (yang2022_guidewire p. 1287; Crossref affiliations)
robots.versions: single paper (yang2022_guidewire, ICMA 2022); the robot is described only in its Sec. IV-A
robots.target_anatomy: abdominal-aorta target in a vessel phantom with pumped water at a controlled temperature (Sec. IV-A, IV-C, Figs. 1-2, 7); detection images from the phantom's femoral artery and aortic arch (Sec. IV-B)
robots.devices_driven: one guidewire (type N.R.)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2: push-pull and rotation, decoupled (Sec. IV-A)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller: 'It moves the guidewire forward or backward via a pair of friction wheels clamping it' (Sec. IV-A)
robots.rotation_detail: 'The rotation of the guidewire around the central axis is achieved by a pair of rotating gears' (Sec. IV-A)
robots.force_sensing: none (force from the motor current proposed as future work, Sec. V)
robots.haptics_leader: none: an autonomous SAC agent on a server sends (push-pull, rotation) actions (Sec. IV-A, Fig. 2)
robots.imaging_compat: camera above the transparent phantom; the YOLOv5s tip detector was also run on angiographic images (Fig. 5); fluoroscopy with the robot N.R.
robots.validation_detail: phantom: two training-and-test experiments on the physical phantom, (1) push-pull only, 500 episodes of <= 150 steps in 2.5 h, converged after about 260 episodes; (2) push-pull plus rotation, 500 episodes in 4.2 h, converged after about 300; test runs reached the target within the 40-pixel (about 5 mm) termination criterion (Sec. IV-C, Figs. 8-13). Number of test runs N.R.
robots.key_numbers: push-pull accuracy 1 mm, rotation accuracy 5 deg (Sec. IV-A); action limits +/-20 mm, +/-90 deg (Sec. III-A); feeding error < 5 mm, tip detection >= 92.9 % (Abstract); YOLOv5s 23 ms per image (Sec. IV-B)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found: the policy is trained on the physical phantom without a simulator ('To avoid the error caused by the virtual simulation environment, we built an interventional surgery experimental platform based on vessel phantom', Sec. IV-A)

robots.name: CSTAR active catheter
robots.full_name: CSTAR robot-assisted active-catheter insertion test bed (7-DOF PA10-7C arm inserting an SMA-actuated catheter)
robots.group: Western University / Canadian Surgical Technologies and Advanced Robotics (CSTAR) (R. V. Patel; J. Jayender, M. Azizian) with NRC Integrated Manufacturing Technologies Institute (S. Nikumb, SMA micro-welding)
robots.versions: 2006 ICRA hybrid impedance (force/position) control of catheter insertion by a 7-DOF redundant robot with proximal force sensing (title; rafiitari2014_current Sec. Robotic platforms); 2007 IROS autonomous insertion with image guidance (title); 2008 TRO autonomous image-guided insertion (full); 2008 BioRob wave-variable bilateral teleoperation of the active catheter (title); 2009 IJRR augmented hybrid impedance control + master-slave SMA tip control (full, jayender2009_robot)
robots.target_anatomy: vascular/angioplasty access (vinyl-tube vessel test bed); PCI-size (5 Fr) catheters as motivation
robots.devices_driven: one 5 Fr guide catheter (Medtronic) instrumented with SMA actuators: three SMA wires at 120 deg, several sections (TRO 2008 Sec. II, VII)
robots.n_dof_detail: 7 (Mitsubishi PA10-7C arm) plus SMA tip bending (yaw and pitch)
robots.translation_detail: other: 7-DOF industrial arm (Mitsubishi PA10-7C) inserts the catheter in strokes whose length is set from image feedback
robots.rotation_detail: arm wrist (catheter roll use N.R.); tip steering by SMA actuators
robots.force_sensing: ATI Gamma 6-DOF wrist force/torque sensor regulates insertion force (TRO 2008 Sec. II)
robots.haptics_leader: none in TRO 2008 (clinician sets start and target in a GUI); IJRR 2009: Phantom Omni gives yaw/pitch references for the SMA tip (closed loop on an NDI Aurora tip sensor, 30 Hz) and the user sets the insertion stroke (Sec. 3.2, 5.4, Fig. 4); bilateral wave-variable teleoperation in BioRob 2008 (title only)
robots.imaging_compat: camera images of the test bed as X-ray stand-in (about 1.0 mm/pixel) plus 5-DOF NDI Aurora EM sensor at the tip (TRO 2008 Sec. II-III)
robots.validation_detail: autonomous insertion through a vinyl-tube test bed with tubes of 3.0, 4.5 and 6.0 mm internal diameter and two bifurcations (second at a random 3-D angle) (TRO 2008 Sec. II, VIII); IJRR 2009: position, force, and force+moment control runs in the 3.0 mm tube, then a teleoperated run through two active branches (left, then right) with SMA bending at each junction (Sec. 5, Figs. 7-20)
robots.key_numbers: arm Cartesian tracking RMS 0.27/0.30/0.43 mm (x/y/z) and 0.18/0.06/0.17 deg; force tracking RMS 0.05 N; host-arm loop 333 Hz; EM sensor RMS 0.9-1.3 mm (TRO 2008 Sec. II, VI); insertion force regulated at 0.25 N, never exceeded through two active branches (IJRR 2009 Sec. 5.4, Fig. 20)

robots.name: CathNav
robots.full_name: CathNav / Althea I and Althea II: 3-DOF robots for semi-automatic and automatic navigation of steerable EP catheters
robots.group: Ryerson University (now Toronto Metropolitan University; F. Janabi-Sharifi) with University of Waterloo (Y. Ganji) and St. Michael's Hospital (A. N. Cheema)
robots.versions: 2009 IJCARS CathNav, called Althea I by the group (norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 1, ref. 14): Velmex linear stage + two rotary stages, stepper motors, 3 swine; 2021 Artif. Organs Althea II (norouzighazbi2021_design, full): three HerkuleX DRS-0602 smart servos for twist, translation and knob bending (Sec. 2.2.1-2.2.2) on an inclined 3D-printed arm (SLS nylon + FDM) riding a Macron MSA-R6S belt-driven linear actuator (325 mm travel, up to 6230 mm/s), customisable handle parts for other catheters, guidewires and sheaths, magnetic stainless-steel shaft holders, gearbox and external bearings removed, portable, assembly 20 min, five times faster than Althea I, two units can cooperate (Sec. 2.2, Figs. 2-3, 11); the 2024 grip-insert-release follower of the same group is robots_A3 toronto_nazari2024
robots.target_anatomy: right atrium (intracardiac EP navigation)
robots.devices_driven: one bidirectional steerable ablation catheter SteeroCath-T (Boston Scientific): 7 Fr shaft, 8 Fr tip, 110 cm (ganji2009 Sec. System setup); Althea II: EP catheters with rotational knobs, swappable handle holder parts for other handles, guidewires and sheaths (norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 2.2.1)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (insertion/retraction, handle twist, knob deflection)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (2009: Velmex linear stage moves the handle, telescopic tubing keeps the external shaft straight; 2021: belt-driven linear actuator carries the handle holder, norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 2.2.2)
robots.rotation_detail: two rotary stages: one twists the handle, one turns the steering knob
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: Novint Falcon 3-D haptic device as input (force feedback N.R.); CathNav GUI
robots.imaging_compat: NDI Aurora EM tracking, two sensors on the distal shaft; fluoroscopy
robots.validation_detail: 3 swine (St. Michael's Hospital vivarium); catheter introduced manually into the right atrium then mounted on the robot; automatic navigation to EM-sensor targets (high RA, tricuspid annulus) (ganji2009 Sec. Experiments setup, Results); Althea II 2021: bench accuracy/repeatability in positioning and velocity modes, comparison with Althea I, cooperative two-robot object manipulation, mitral-valve and clip grasping inside an artificial heart model, image-based visual servoing; no in vivo test (norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 3-4)
robots.key_numbers: mean distance to target 6.53 mm, all trials below 10 mm (ganji2009 Abstract, Results); Althea II: > 90 % accuracy in velocity and positioning modes, about 2.5x more accurate and 6x more repeatable than Althea I (Table 5), cooperative object path error 0.299 mm, YOLO tip detection MSE 0.05 mm (Table 4), assembly 18 / 23 / 17 min by three people (norouzighazbi2021)

robots.name: CathROB
robots.full_name: CathROB remote catheter navigation system (with its 2007-2008 telerobotic predecessor)
robots.group: University of Bologna, Laboratory of Bioengineering (L. Cercenelli, E. Marcelli, G. Plicchi, B. Bortolani), developed with Tre Esse Progettazione Biomedica
robots.versions: 2007 ASAIO J telerobotic system (cercenelli2007_initial, full): driving unit on an articulation arm giving advance/withdrawal, rotation and tip steering to a standard EP catheter, PIC16F876 control unit at the bedside, remote push-button box with display (wired or wireless), automatic repositioning to stored targets (Methods, Figs. 1-2); 2008 Computers in Cardiology telerobotic system with force sensing (title); 2017 CathROB: mock handle plus push-button box, compact arm-mounted Motion Unit (full)
robots.target_anatomy: cardiac electrophysiology mapping and RF ablation (right atrium in sheep; silicone left-atrium model)
robots.devices_driven: one standard tip-steerable EP catheter; adapters for Navistar Thermocool and EZ-steer bidirectional (Biosense Webster), Sprinklr XL 7 Fr (Medtronic), Blazer II XP (Boston Scientific); tested with Navistar Thermocool 4 mm 7.5 Fr (Sec. 2.1); 2007: RF Enhancr steerable EP catheter (Medtronic) (cercenelli2007 Methods)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (advance/withdraw, rotation, tip bend/straighten)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (Motion Unit moves the handle held by a spring-preloaded jaw block with silicone-coated rollers; Delrin telescopic sheath to the introducer)
robots.rotation_detail: DC micromotor rotates the gripped handle; steering element turned through catheter-specific adapters
robots.device_range: four commercial EP catheter models via adapters
robots.footprint_mm: Motion Unit 53 x 8 x 11 cm (Fig. 4 labels; text prints 53 x 8 x 110 cm) retracted, 73 x 8 x 11 cm extended (Sec. 2.1)
robots.force_sensing: Honeywell FS-series piezoresistive sensor in the push path; alarm at 60% and stop at 80% of a perforation force of 128 +- 12 gF measured on excised ovine atrium (Sec. 2.1)
robots.haptics_leader: mock catheter handle plus push-button box; vibration motor and acoustic alarm when thresholds are exceeded; up to four stored targets for automatic repositioning
robots.imaging_compat: standard fluoroscopy and CARTO electroanatomic mapping; operator outside the radiation field
robots.sterility: disposable or sterilisable adapters; Motion Unit and arm draped in sterile polyethylene in vivo
robots.validation_detail: in vitro silicone heart and vascular mock-up; in vivo 4 sheep (49 +- 4 kg) with right-atrial CARTO mapping and RF ablation at RA isthmus and posterior wall (Sec. 2.2, 3); 2007 predecessor: 3 sheep (58 +- 3 kg), navigation and repositioning to 12 predefined endocardial targets under fluoroscopy, manual vs robotic (cercenelli2007 Methods, Results)
robots.key_numbers: automatic repositioning error 1.5 +- 0.6 mm (left targets) and 1.7 +- 0.5 mm (right; abstract 1.7 +- 0.4); map-to-CT deviation 1.37 +- 0.98 mm; in vivo set-up 5 +- 3 min, maps 63 +- 8 points in 36 +- 7 min with 15 +- 3 min fluoroscopy; speeds 13-18 mm/s, 30-45 deg/s, 2-4 mm/s; no perforation or rhythm change (Sec. 2.1, 3); 2007: navigation 13.0 +- 5.6 s robotic vs 16.1 +- 6.4 s manual, repositioning 9.2 +- 2.5 vs 17.8 +- 7.1 s (both p < 0.001); bench repositioning accuracy 0.2 +- 0.1 mm, 1.4 +- 0.8 mm, 2.1 +- 0.9 mm (longitudinal, rotational, steering) (cercenelli2007 Abstract, Methods)

robots.name: Motion-comp. catheter
robots.full_name: Harvard motion-compensation catheter system (voice-coil guidewire drive with 3-D ultrasound servoing)
robots.group: Harvard SEAS BioRobotics Lab (R. D. Howe; S. B. Kesner)
robots.versions: 2011 ICRA force control of flexible catheter robots for beating-heart surgery (title); 2011 TRO position control with friction and backlash compensation (full, PMC author manuscript); 2014 IJRR robotic catheter cardiac ablation combining 3DUS guidance and force control, new force-sensing RF ablation end effector (full, kesner2014_robotic)
robots.target_anatomy: intracardiac beating-heart repair (mitral annulus tracking); RF cardiac ablation (kesner2014 Sec. 1-2)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire/instrument sliding in a fixed 85 cm Teflon sheath with steel spring; in vivo 1.5 mm OD guidewire in 1.6 mm ID sheath (TRO 2011 Sec. III, Table I)
robots.n_dof_detail: 1 actuated (fast axial translation); bending and rotation by the clinician with conventional catheter controls
robots.translation_detail: other: voice-coil linear actuator (H2W NCC20-18-02-1X, 50.8 mm travel, 26.7 N peak) on a BX3-3 linear ball slide
robots.rotation_detail: none (manual); pull-wire bending and guidewire twisting proposed as future DOF (Fig. 18)
robots.device_range: sheath ID 1.59-2.38 mm with guidewire OD 0.76-2.23 mm tested (Table I)
robots.force_sensing: LCFD-1KG load cell (10 N range) in the drive measures friction; LP-50F potentiometer for position (TRO 2011); IJRR 2014: catheter-tip force sensor, a reflective surface on perpendicular 0.25 mm NiTi flexures read by a fibre-optic transducer, 3D-printed (Objet Connex500), about 5 mm diameter, integrated with the RF ablation electrode, calibrated against an ATI Mini40 (Sec. 2.2, Figs. 4-5)
robots.haptics_leader: linear joystick adds commands to the fast axis; no force feedback reported
robots.imaging_compat: 3-D ultrasound (Philips SONOS 7500, epicardial) with GPU Radon-transform tool tracking; EKF compensates 50-100 ms imaging delay
robots.validation_detail: one 75 kg pig, catheter inserted through the top of the left atrium (not through the vasculature), mitral-annulus tracking trials longer than 15 s; number of trials N.R. (TRO 2011 Sec. VII); IJRR 2014: bench force-control runs and water-tank runs under 3DUS against a target moving 12 mm at about 1 Hz (sinusoid and human mitral-annulus trajectory), robotic vs manual Medtronic RF Marinr MCXL catheter (Sec. 4-5, Figs. 16-17)
robots.key_numbers: in vivo RMS tracking error below 1.0 mm in all trials (0.77 mm shown) vs above 8 mm without compensation; friction compensation up to 2 N; bench MAE 1.28 -> 0.26 mm (inverse compensation, 1 Hz) and 2.34 -> 0.24 mm (model-based); design targets >= 20 mm travel, >= 210 mm/s, >= 3800 mm/s^2, about 4 N (TRO 2011); IJRR 2014: 1 N contact force held on the moving target under 3DUS with 0.08 N RMS error, 97 % less RMS contact-resistance variation than the manual catheter, force control improved motion tracking by about 20 % (Abstract)

robots.group: Harvard SEAS (R. D. Howe; P. M. Loschak, A. Degirmenci) with MIT Lincoln Laboratory (L. J. Brattain) and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (C. M. Tschabrunn, E. Anter)
robots.versions: 2017 TRO algorithms for automatically pointing ICE catheters, benchtop (full, PMC author manuscript); 2020 IJRR in-vivo automatic steering with respiratory motion compensation (full, loschak2020_automatically); earlier in vivo navigation study Degirmenci et al. 2016 (cited in loschak2020 Sec. 1, not read)
robots.target_anatomy: intracardiac echocardiography in the heart chambers
robots.devices_driven: AcuNav 10 Fr (3.30 mm) 110 cm ICE catheter with 64-element array (Biosense Webster) (TRO 2017 Sec. II)
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 (pitch knob, yaw knob, handle roll, handle translation)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (lead-screw translation stage carries the whole handle)
robots.rotation_detail: motor grounded to the stage turns the handle by timing belt; two handle-mounted motors turn the knobs by timing belts
robots.force_sensing: none reported
robots.haptics_leader: none (automatic target-based steering)
robots.imaging_compat: ICE ultrasound; EM tracking of instrument tip in tests; IJRR 2020: four EM trackers (two on the US catheter, one on the target catheter, one on the chest wall for respiration) (Sec. 3.2)

robots.full_name: SETA (System for Endovascular Teleoperated Access)
robots.group: State University of New York (SUNY) at Buffalo, Dept. of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (G. Srimathveeravalli, T. Kesavadas, X. Li)
robots.versions: 2010 IJMRCAS (full); the same PI's later SAER robot (UIUC/Buffalo) is robots_A3 saer_sankaran2018; Ashammagari et al. 2016 IMECE automated aortic-arch access on the VIST simulator used a 7-DOF Robai Cyton arm, neither SETA nor SAER (ashammagari2016_image, full)
robots.target_anatomy: neurovascular / endovascular access (design data from femoral-to-internal-carotid angiograms in rabbits and on VIST; srimathveeravalli2010_design Materials and Methods)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire and catheter simultaneously, any standard device 0.014-0.13 in (friction-wheel range); bench: 0.035 in guidewire + 5 Fr Boston Scientific Expo catheter (Results); VIST trial: the manual angiogram (0.035 / 0.014 in Emerald guidewires, 5 Fr Tempo Aqua catheter) repeated with SETA
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 motorised: guidewire insert/withdraw, catheter insert/withdraw, catheter twist (three Maxon EC-22 motors); a travelling cart carrying the guidewire drive and the steering stage runs on a pulley (Design of patient-side slave, Actuators; Fig. 2)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller: driven lower + idler upper 2 in polyurethane wheels (Shore 55A, mu ~0.6), spring-tensioned self-adjusting housing, normal load 1.275 N (Slave actuators; Fig. 3)
robots.rotation_detail: catheter only: miniature gripper of brass roller pins on O-ring-tensioned steel shafts (transmits torque, allows axial slip) turned by a pulley from a servomotor and torque sensor (Slave actuators; Fig. 4)
robots.force_sensing: proximal: LXT 971 torque sensor (Cooper Instruments, +/-2.5 Nm, 0.005 Nm resolution) between each motor and its wheel/pulley, converted to axial and radial tool forces (Slave actuators; Teleoperation)
robots.haptics_leader: Novint Falcon; twist mapped to left-right stylus motion; force-reflecting loop at 500 Hz with Butterworth tremor filter (5-25 Hz), motion scaling and delay term (Teleoperation and haptic feedback, Eq. 1, Fig. 5)
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.validation_detail: bench: step inputs to 30/60/90 mm at 1000/2500/5000 rpm, 15 repeats each, plus ramps (Fig. 6); steering 1 deg steps over 360 deg, 10 cycles each way on a 5 F catheter (Fig. 7); phantom: teleoperated 0.035 in guidewire in a silicone vessel with one bifurcation (Fig. 8); VIST simulator: 8 neurovascular surgeons and fellows (7 M, 1 F, mean 500 cases) repeated a carotid angiogram, procedure time 87.42 s robotic vs 80.57 s manual (p = 0.829), contrast 7 vs 5.75 cc (p = 0.723), 1 participant did not finish; questionnaire 2.25-3.0 of 4 (Table 3, Fig. 11). In vivo animal studies only planned (Abstract, Conclusion)
robots.key_numbers: insertion slip < 0.4 mm per 100 mm; teleoperated phantom lag < 0.003 in; back-slip force 0.76 N (4x below the 3 N tool limit, so buckling stays outside the lumen); EC-22 motors 18,000 rpm max with 1:128 gearhead (~3 Nm); friction-wheel assembly 130 g; teleoperation 500 Hz; master spec from motion study: 28.5 mm stroke, 4.5 N, 13 Hz hand motion (Slave actuators, Teleoperation, Results)
robots.sim_model: none found (VIST simulator used as the test patient, not a model of SETA)

robots.name: ROSES
robots.full_name: ROSES (RObotic System for Endovascular Surgery)
robots.group: Calabrian High Tech (CHT S.r.l.; G. Danieli) with Magna Graecia University (C. Indolfi, A. Polimeni, S. De Rosa)
robots.versions: 2018 PCT patent (ref. 6 of indolfi2023_first); robot actuator v1 (motor axes parallel to the gear train), v2 (motors perpendicular, thinner), v3 (36 mm central passage for haemostasis valve and large catheters) (danieli2022_development Fig. 12); disposables for angioplasty (DA), big catheters (DEBC), movable-core guidewires and a tip-curvature catheter; cart with rail and force transducer for endovascular surgery (Fig. 13); first patient 22 Jan 2019; 2023 case report
robots.target_anatomy: coronary PCI; endovascular surgery, large catheters for aneurysm repair or TAVI (cart version)
robots.devices_driven: guidewire plus balloon or stent catheter per slave; first-in-human: 6 Fr JR4 guide, 0.014 in BMW wire, 2.0 x 12 mm balloon, 2.5 x 15 mm DES (indolfi2023_first)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 per slave (catheter advance/retract, guidewire advance/retract, common rotation); one console drives up to three slaves (techbriefs 2019 entry)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (3-D-printed disposables convert gear rotation into advance/retract through friction wheels)
robots.rotation_detail: the disposable is rotated by a concentric gear train in the robot actuator (danieli2022_development Sec. 2)
robots.device_range: 0.014 in guidewires to large catheters (36 mm passage in v3); exact Fr range N.R.
robots.force_sensing: resistance to advancement shown on the console; cart version measures forces opposed by the patient with a force transducer (danieli2022_development abstract, Sec. 3)
robots.haptics_leader: passive master console with joysticks per track (one for the guidewire, one for devices); no force rendering reported
robots.imaging_compat: fluoroscopy; cockpit inside or outside the cath lab
robots.sterility: sterile disposables in contact with the devices, split upper/lower so they can be removed without withdrawing the device (danieli2022_development abstract)
robots.validation_detail: in vitro tubing and X-ray tests; first patient 22 Jan 2019 (two stents), trials 'still in progress' in 2022 (danieli2022_development Sec. 2); 2023 case report of one 64-year-old patient (R-PCI of a PL branch)
robots.key_numbers: case: procedure 35 min, contrast 110 mL, stent result satisfactory at 2.5-year follow-up (indolfi2023_first); fluoroscopy time N.R.

robots.name: RNS
robots.full_name: Remote Navigation System (RNS)
robots.group: NaviCath Ltd. (R. Beyar co-founder) with Rambam Medical Center / Technion; clinical sites also Fundeni Hospital and Shaare Zedek (beyar2006_remote p. 296-297)
robots.versions: 2005 concept, design and pre-clinical studies (EuroIntervention 2005;1:340-5, cited as weisz2013_safety ref. 1; not read); 2006 JACC first-in-human pilot (beyar2006_remote); described as the basis of CorPath 200 (crinnion2022_robotics; no full text states that NaviCath became Corindus)
robots.target_anatomy: coronary PCI
robots.devices_driven: standard 0.014-in coronary guidewire and the angioplasty device (balloon or stent); the guiding catheter is hooked to the RNS but not driven; the two devices are interlocked: 'When the guidewire is manipulated, the device is locked at its position and vice versa' (beyar2006_remote p. 296-297). Rapid-exchange devices per wagener2024_features (not stated in beyar2006)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3: wire axial and rotation (optionally discrete 30-degree steps), device axial (beyar2006_remote p. 296)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (device: motored roller pair with a passive motion-sensing roller pair behind it, beyar2006_remote p. 296, Fig. 2B; wire: 'mechanical transmission module', type N.R.)
robots.rotation_detail: wire navigator rotates the wire through a mechanical transmission module (type N.R.) (beyar2006_remote p. 296)
robots.force_sensing: no force sensor named: motion-sensing rollers report slippage of the motored rollers and the system halts; 'any force that exceeds a threshold causes system stall' (beyar2006_remote p. 296, 299)
robots.haptics_leader: no: computerised touch-screen control console and joystick (beyar2006_remote p. 296, Fig. 3); haptic force feedback named as future work (p. 299)
robots.imaging_compat: standard fluoroscopy screens; the protocol kept the operators at the bedside (beyar2006_remote p. 299)
robots.sterility: detachable wire and device navigators on a sterile plastic-sheet-covered base; Y-connector in a sterile holder (beyar2006_remote p. 296, Fig. 2 caption); disposable status N.R.
robots.validation_detail: glass coronary model; anaesthetised sheep (number N.R.), 14 coronary branches, 8 stents implanted; first-in-human pilot: 18 patients (15 men, 3 women) at 3 centres, single-vessel PCI (beyar2006_remote p. 297); 20 lesions per wagener2024_features Table 1 (lesion count not stated in beyar2006)
robots.key_numbers: wire crossed the lesion in 17 of 18; stent delivered in 15 of 17; technical success 94% (guidewire) and 83% (overall procedure); clinical success 100%; fluoroscopy time 8.8 +- 4.8 vs 9.1 +- 3.5 min with standard technique (NS); catheterisation time 44 +- 32.7 vs 61 +- 19 min; diameter stenosis 60.6 +- 13.5% -> 17.0 +- 7.8%; no in-hospital MACE (beyar2006_remote p. 296-298)

robots.name: MitraClip stabiliser
robots.full_name: PoliMi motorised stabiliser for the MitraClip delivery catheter with IRL path planning
robots.group: Politecnico di Milano, DEIB NEARLab (E. De Momi; X. Zhang, A. Segato) with E. Votta (cardiovascular biomechanics); Horizon 2020 funding
robots.versions: 2022 IROS (only)
robots.target_anatomy: structural heart: transseptal mitral edge-to-edge repair
robots.devices_driven: Abbott MitraClip delivery catheter, 16 Fr (5.28 mm), 109.5 cm, three pull wires 90 deg apart, inside its sheath (Sec. III-C)
robots.n_dof_detail: 3 (medio-lateral bending, antero-posterior bending, insertion in the sheath)
robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (linear actuator on the motorised stabiliser advances the delivery catheter)
robots.rotation_detail: none; two bending DOF actuated through the handle
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: none (autonomous execution of planned path, PID on EM feedback)
robots.imaging_compat: NDI Aurora EM: 5-DOF tip sensor (0.7 +- 1.4 mm) for feedback, 6-DOF probe (0.48 +- 0.88 mm) for recording
robots.validation_detail: patient-specific silicone phantom of femoral vein and IVC with rigid fossa ovalis and mitral replicas registered to Unity (Sec. IV-A)
robots.key_numbers: closed-loop tip error 1.12 +- 0.75, 1.09 +- 0.68, 1.66 +- 0.62 mm (X/Y/Z), maximum 2.64 mm; PID reduces mean error by 32.68% vs open loop; planned path 60.63 +- 0.96 mm (BC+GAIL) vs 64.99 +- 6.11 mm (manual) (Sec. V)

robots.name: Caranx TAVI robot
robots.full_name: Caranx Medical robotic instrument manipulator for transcatheter aortic valve implantation
robots.group: Caranx Medical (P. Berthet-Rayne, J. Smits, P. Schegg) with Institut Arnault Tzanck, Clinique Pasteur, Emory University, University Hospital Nice
robots.versions: Oct 2023 hybrid-room phantom tests; Dec 2023 - Feb 2024 three in-vivo porcine experiments (CERIMED Marseille); 15 Mar 2024 robot-assisted TAV implantation in a pig; 2025 FRAI paper
robots.target_anatomy: transfemoral TAVI (aortic valve)
robots.devices_driven: Edwards SAPIEN 3 delivery system (flex catheter and handle), intraventricular guidewire, balloon inflation device (Results, Fig. 2)
robots.n_dof_detail: N.R. as a number; four drivers: catheter driver, handle driver (flex and balloon fine-positioning wheels), guidewire driver, inflation driver
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (friction-wheel transmissions for delivery catheter and guidewire, pretensioned by one screw)
robots.rotation_detail: handle wheels through geared transmissions; catheter roll N.R.
robots.device_range: one delivery-system type per interface (a reusable base with per-device interfaces envisioned)
robots.force_sensing: in-line pressure sensor for pressure-monitored balloon inflation; instrument force sensing N.R.
robots.haptics_leader: single wireless handheld user-input device; teleoperation from a shielded room
robots.imaging_compat: fluoroscopy (wireless pedal) and camera test bench; neural-network feature tracking for closed-loop positioning
robots.sterility: plastic transmission covers on handle wheels; quick-release thumbscrews and spring-loaded sliders; N.R. further
robots.validation_detail: 3 in-vivo porcine experiments with 20 navigation and balloon-inflation sequences (no implant) and one robot-assisted TAV implantation in a pig; phantom operator study and level-3 supervised autonomy with camera and fluoroscopy feedback (Results)
robots.key_numbers: fluoroscopy closed-loop positioning 30 runs without failure, final error 0.5 mm median, min-max range 1.03 mm; calibration about 5 s; autonomy up to 2x accuracy and 4x precision vs manual on phantom (Results)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found (network trained on real fluoroscopy data)

robots.name: Hamlyn driver
robots.full_name: Hamlyn hands-on robotic catheter driver for learning from demonstration (pre-CathBot)
robots.group: Imperial College London, Hamlyn Centre (G.-Z. Yang; H. Rafii-Tari, W. Chi, C. J. Payne, J. Liu, C. Riga, C. Bicknell)
robots.versions: 2012 IROS force-feedback system for catheterisation (Payne, title only); 2013 MICCAI GMM/GMR learning with the driver; 2014 MICCAI hierarchical-HMM cooperative catheterisation; 2018 IJCARS non-rigid-registration trajectory transfer; from 2020 the Hamlyn LfD work runs on CathBot (chi2020_collaborative uses 'the CathBot system')
robots.target_anatomy: aortic arch cannulation (innominate, left common carotid) in silicone phantoms
robots.devices_driven: one standard catheter (operator handles the guidewire manually in the 2013 shared-control scheme)
robots.n_dof_detail: 2 (axial, rotational)
robots.translation_detail: friction-roller (pair of friction wheels coupled to one servomotor)
robots.rotation_detail: second servomotor rotates the frame that holds the catheter; two Dynamixel MX-28 servomotors, PID (rafiitari2013 Sec. 2.3; chi2018 Sec. Experiments)
robots.force_sensing: none on the driver; ATI Mini40 6-DOF sensor under the phantom for evaluation (chi2018)
robots.haptics_leader: hands-on master: proximal position-sensing unit that reads natural catheter motions (two DOF); no force feedback in these papers
robots.imaging_compat: NDI Aurora 6-DOF EM sensor at the tip; 2-D projected image for the operator
robots.validation_detail: 2013: 12 robotic cannulations per learned model (expert and intermediate) across 4 inexperienced operators; 2018: cross-validation over three type-I aortic-arch phantoms under dry, continuous and pulsatile flow, forces vs four experts
robots.key_numbers: 2018 success 98.1% dry and 94.4% continuous flow; mean contact force -33.3% and force SD -70.6% vs manual (chi2018 abstract)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found (policies learned from real phantom demonstrations)

robots.name: SMA ablation cath.
robots.full_name: NC State SMA-actuated robotic ablation catheter (Buckner lab)
robots.group: North Carolina State University, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Electro-Mechanics Research Laboratory (G. D. Buckner; J. H. Crews, J. H. Wiest); NIH SBIR 5R44HL095227 (no company named)
robots.versions: 2008 Veeramani, Buckner et al.: modelling (Smart Mater. Struct.) and design and control (ASME DSCC) of an SMA-actuated robotic catheter, cited by crews2012 and wiest2015 (not read); 2012 JIMSS design optimisation of single-tendon and antagonistic SMA segments in COMSOL with a genetic algorithm, tested on planar wire rigs (crews2012_design, full); 2015 RAS path optimisation and control of a two-segment, eight-tendon catheter (wiest2015_path, full); the lab's later bedside robot is robots_A3 portable_kantu2025 (NC State/NYU), predecessor of LegoBot
robots.target_anatomy: endocardial RF ablation (left atrium)
robots.devices_driven: own 2.7 mm catheter with two bending segments, each actuated by four offset SMA tendons (wiest2015 Sec. 2)
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 bending (two segments x bend angle and orientation)
robots.translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation (SMA tendons heated by PWM); no robotic insertion stage
robots.rotation_detail: none
robots.device_range: 90 and 180 degrees of omnidirectional bending for the proximal and distal segments (wiest2015_path p. 93); own 2.7 mm catheter
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: joystick on the catheter handle
robots.imaging_compat: modified EnSite NavX (St. Jude) electrode localisation (wiest2015_path p. 94); trakSTAR magnetic tracking on the 2012 test rigs (crews2012_design p. 552)
robots.validation_detail: bench: catheter submerged in a saline tank with EnSite patch electrodes; path optimisation repeated on four point sets; closed-loop control on one optimised 16-point path (wiest2015_path pp. 95-96); 2012: single-tendon rig (4 tendon offsets x 11 prestrains, 5 tests each) and four antagonistic rigs (crews2012_design p. 552-553)
robots.key_numbers: path optimisation about 20 s; step response about 2 s with < 10 deg overshoot; mean steady-state tip error 5.5 mm, called unacceptably large by the authors; NavX uncertainty 7.1 +- 3.5 mm, imprecision +- 0.8 mm (wiest2015_path); 2012: optimal bend radius 7.0 mm (single-crystal model) and 7.6 mm (polycrystalline); experimental optimum prestrain about 3.5-4.5% and tendon offset about 1 mm (crews2012_design p. 555-556)
robots.sim_model: yes: COMSOL finite-element models of SMA-actuated segments coupled to a genetic algorithm in MATLAB (single-crystal and polycrystalline free-energy SMA models), checked on wire rigs (crews2012_design p. 546-557); MATLAB simulations to tune the 2015 path optimiser (wiest2015_path Sec. 2.6)
robots.sim2real_detail: none found (simulation used for design optimisation, not for a controller)

robots.name: ICE manipulator
robots.full_name: Siemens Healthineers robotic ICE catheter manipulator (proximal and distal units)
robots.group: Siemens Healthineers Digital Technology & Innovation (Y.-H. Kim, A. Kapoor, T. Mansi) with Houston Methodist (C. H. Lin, Z. Li) and Texas A&M (R. Langari, zero-slack design)
robots.versions: 2020 arXiv (kim2020_towards: 'Back' unit on the handle turns both knobs and gives bulk rotation, 'Front' unit at the introducer gives translation and rotation; 3 pig experiments) / 2022 IJCARS 4-DOF manipulator with automated view recovery (distal and proximal units; 4 pig experiments); 2022 arXiv zero-slack separable ICE robot (debuy2022_design: reusable back portion with four Faulhaber LM 1483-080-11-C linear motors pulling the four tendons directly through 3:1 spools, disposable front portion clipped on with a twist lock and magnetic coupling; 2 bending DOF only, translation/rotation not handled; Materials and Methods, Fig. 1); 2025 arXiv tip-visibility guidance (title)
robots.target_anatomy: intracardiac echocardiography during EP and structural-heart procedures (incl. transseptal puncture)
robots.devices_driven: ACUSON AcuNav Volume ICE catheters (Siemens Healthineers)
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 (two knob angles, bulk rotation, translation)
robots.translation_detail: other: proximal unit at the introducer sheath gives linear and rotational motion of the shaft (mechanism N.R.)
robots.rotation_detail: distal unit holds the handle, turns both knobs and gives bulk rotation synchronised with the proximal unit
robots.footprint_mm: zero-slack version: 298 mm long, 66 mm diameter (debuy2022 Fig. 1(a) dimension labels); 2020/2022 manipulator N.R.
robots.force_sensing: none
robots.haptics_leader: 6-DOF analog joystick, no force feedback
robots.imaging_compat: ICE ultrasound; fluoroscopy-free robot-guided transseptal punctures in animals
robots.sterility: zero-slack version: reusable actuator back portion, disposable front portion that holds the catheter tendons (debuy2022 Introduction, Fig. 1); 2020/2022 manipulator N.R.
robots.validation_detail: 4 animal experiments (pig, Houston Methodist MITIE) including 2 fluoro-less robot-guided transseptal punctures; beating-heart phantom (Archetype Medical) (kim2022 Sec. 3)
robots.key_numbers: view recovery 2.09 +- 0.90 mm and 3.93 +- 2.07 deg in animals, 0.67 +- 0.79 mm and 0.37 +- 0.19 deg in phantom (kim2022 abstract); bench compensation at 60 deg bend 14.8 mm / 31.0 deg -> 5.0 mm / 10.3 deg RMSE (kim2020 arXiv); zero-slack bench, 3 sinusoid trials: tip MAE 4.80 mm / 6.11 deg, 3.31 mm / 3.26 deg with +/-10 deg hysteresis compensation (debuy2022 Table 1)

robots.name: CardioXplorer
robots.full_name: CardioXplorer open-source modular teleoperated robotic catheter-ablation system
robots.group: King's College London, School of Biomedical Engineering & Imaging Sciences (K. S. Rhode, R. J. Housden; Z. Xu, A. M. Zeidan) with Guy's and St Thomas' and St George's hospitals
robots.versions: 2024 MDPI Robotics (only); sibling KCL robot for transseptal puncture (kcl_tsp_zeidan2023)
robots.target_anatomy: atrial-fibrillation catheter ablation (pulmonary vein isolation)
robots.devices_driven: commercial ablation catheters through a catheter-agnostic handle gripper: Thermocool SmartTouch SF and CS, Webster CS EZ Steer (Biosense Webster), Blazer II XP (Boston Scientific) (Sec. 2.1)

robots.translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (linear module: NEMA-17 stepper with GT2 belt drive carries the handle, 220 mm insertion depth)
robots.rotation_detail: NEMA-8 stepper (19:1) rotates the handle without limit through a slip ring; servo (12 kg.cm holding torque) turns the knob +-60 deg

robots.force_sensing: none on the robot (knob torque of about 6 kg.cm measured during design)

robots.validation_detail: benchtop targeting of left pulmonary veins in an AF-patient cardiac phantom; 3 cardiologists and 2 trainees, 5 trials, manual vs robot (Sec. 3)
robots.key_numbers: task duration -1.59 s with the robot; robotic motion 35.2% smoother for experts than intermediates; jerk improvement vs manual 42.2% (experts) and 13.6% (intermediates); speeds up to +-25 mm/s, 0.5 deg rotation steps up to 9.375 rps; parts cost about USD 700 (abstract, Sec. 2)

robots.name: TMVR delivery
robots.full_name: Georgia Tech telerobotic transcatheter delivery system for a mitral valve implant
robots.group: Georgia Institute of Technology, RoboMed Laboratory (J. P. Desai; R. Qi, N. U. Nayar)
robots.versions: 2020 IROS first robotic transcatheter delivery system (title); ICRA 2021, T-MRB 2022 and ICRA 2023 papers of Nayar, Qi and Desai (qi2023 refs. [18]-[20], not read); 2023 RAL telerobotic system: reinforced guide tube in a 24 Fr commercial steerable sheath, stronger actuation, waterproofing, stabiliser, wireless joystick (qi2023, full)
robots.target_anatomy: mitral valve (transseptal implant delivery)
robots.devices_driven: own robotic catheter (5.7 mm OD) on a 1.11 m reinforced guide tube inside a customised steerable outer sheath (VERGO, Duke Extrusion; 6.6 mm ID, 8.3 mm OD, 990.6 mm) (qi2023 Abstract, Sec. IV-A)
robots.n_dof_detail: 4 (proximal bending +-90 deg, distal bending +-120 deg, prismatic 70 mm actuatable and restricted to 60 mm, distal torsion +-75 deg; qi2023 Sec. II)
robots.translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation (distal prismatic joint: the quadlumen tube is advanced by a Pololu 100:1 gearmotor through a lead screw on a linear guide; tendon-driven bending and torsion joints; actuation unit on a stabiliser with a linear guide rail; qi2023 Sec. II)
robots.rotation_detail: tendon-driven distal torsion joint: two antagonistic tendons on a lead-screw holder driven by a DC motor with a 16:1 gearbox (qi2023 Sec. II)
robots.force_sensing: none reported
robots.haptics_leader: wireless Xbox 360 controller, no haptics
robots.imaging_compat: N.R.
robots.sterility: N.R.; waterproofed with two three-way stopcocks for saline introduction (qi2023 Sec. II)
robots.validation_detail: implant delivery in a realistic human cardiovascular phantom (United Biologics) with a ViVitro pulsatile pump (63.1 ml/stroke, 70 beats/min), one demonstration; tube validation with the implant free and against the leaflet; no animal study yet (qi2023 Sec. IV-A, IV-B, V)
robots.key_numbers: joint tracking RMSE 0.20, 0.74, 0.02 and 0.17 mm (qi2023 Sec. IV-A); Maxon 0.5 W 8 mm DC motors (64:1 bending, 16:1 torsion) and Pololu 100:1 prismatic gearmotor, tendon force up to about 20 N (Sec. II); implant advanced 40 mm under the leaflet (Sec. IV-A); tip deflection about 2 mm during a 15 s hold (Sec. IV-B)
robots.sim_model: analytical static deflection model of the reinforced quadlumen tube (eqs. 1-10), checked against ANSYS 18.2 FEM and a camera bench test in 12 configurations (qi2023 Sec. III-C, Table I); not a model of the whole robot
